Colgate.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet for Colgate, so every 2025 starter — including outside hitter Milan Bayless (28 starts), middle blocker Maddie Rudolph (27) and middle blocker Lal Akin (26) — is currently unaccounted for rather than confirmed back. The 2025 team went 18-10 across 28 matches with a known lineup, finishing 98th in RPI and 115th in our final ranking. The projection for 2026 is 16.94 wins, with a range from 11 to 22, and a slight bump to 106th in our rank. Patriot title odds sit at 23.0 percent, tournament odds at 30.6 percent.

Colorado.summary: Colorado brings back 88% of its production and five of six starters from a 23-9 season, with the only hole at setter after Rian Finley started all 32 matches in the 5-1. Ana Burilović headlines the returners at 5.433 points per set, ahead of Sydney Jordan (2.962) and middle Cayla Payne (2.756), who also started 32 matches. The Big 12 group finished 22nd in final RPI and is projected for 16.19 wins, with a range from 9 to 23 and a 42.5% shot at the tournament.

Colorado St..summary: All six of last season's primary starters are back, including middle Eve Wilson (3.648 points per set) and outside Maria Brun (3.383), leaving no vacancies in the starting six and 89% of production returning. The departures are real but manageable: Riley Simpson (81 points in 2025) and Jazen Debina (80, now at Cleveland St.) headline six players out, against just one transfer in. That continuity moves the projection to 15.87 wins after a 21-9 season, with a 36.8% shot at the tournament.

Columbia.summary: Columbia brings back five of six starters and 63% of its production after a 2-22 season, with the only vacancy at libero/DS where Presley Liberty departed. All six of the top scorers return, led by outside hitter Elena Maynulet at 3.304 points per set and middle Maria Happ at 2.294. The biggest subtraction is opposite Eva Atkins and her 243.0 points; there are no incoming transfers. The projection is 6.26 wins with a range of 2 to 11, and a rank of 325 after finishing 328th.

Coppin St..summary: Coppin St. went 23-12 last season but has to replace TaKenya Stafford, who scored 550.0 points at outside hitter, along with middle Ahzhi Coleman (175.5) and setter Ayanna Pharoah (143.0). Three of the six regular starters are back, leaving three vacancies, and returning production sits at 52 percent. The top six scorers by points per set are all listed as returning, led by Cherisse Atilano at 3.141 and Kayden Cupid at 2.226, though setter is the obvious hole with Andrea Cintron at 0.775. The projection is 17.82 wins in a range from 11 to 24, with a 19.2 percent tournament chance in the MEAC.

Cornell.summary: The middle blockers are the whole returning offense here: Mackenzie Parsons (3.296 points per set) and Ava Bogan (2.25) are both back after starting all 25 matches, while the top three departures are all outside hitters, led by Eliza Konvicka's 403.5 points. That leaves four vacancies in the starting six and 47 percent of production returning, with no transfers in to fill the pins. After a 15-10 season, the projection is 13.44 wins with a range of 8 to 18 and a 17.4 percent chance at the tournament.

Creighton.summary: Creighton has to rebuild three of six starting spots after losing setter Annalea Maeder, outside hitter Ava Martin and middle blocker Kiara Reinhardt, all of whom started 33 matches in 2025. Martin alone accounted for 595.5 points, and only 44 percent of the team's production returns. What is back is front-row scoring: Jaya Johnson at 2.894 points per set, Abbey Hayes at 2.161 and Eloise Brandewie at 1.975, plus three transfers in. Coming off a 28-6 season and a final RPI of 7, the projection is 21.4 wins with a 90.6 percent tournament chance.

Dartmouth.summary: Dartmouth brings back its top six scorers by points per set, led by Maddie LaFata at 2.75 and Elle McCreery at 1.918, along with setter Sophia Gagnepain, who started 21 matches in the 5-1. The one real hole is outside hitter Kauany Gutz, who started 22 matches and scored 288 points before departing, leaving two starting-six vacancies. Returning production sits at 55 percent with 10 players back, 7 gone and no transfers in. After a 7-17 season and a final RPI of 266, the projection is 6.04 wins with a range of 2 to 11.

Davidson.summary: Davidson brings back 78% of its production and five of six starters from a 12-16 season, with only one vacancy in the starting lineup after Anna Withee's departure. The top six scorers from 2025 are all returning, led by outside hitter Elena Garcia-Guerrios at 4.068 points per set and Meile Songaila at 2.753. Withee's 160 points are the main loss, along with Emma Slusser's 139 from the opposite spot in the 5-1. The projection is 12.65 wins in the Atlantic 10 with a 4.4% tournament chance, a modest step up to a rank of 187 from 210.

Dayton.summary: Eleven players departed after a 23-7 season, including middle Liana Sarkissian (312.0 points) and setter Viktoria Wahlgren (188.5), leaving three of six starting spots open and 49% of production returning. Kamryn Hunt is the anchor that stayed, leading the team at 4.519 points per set with 28 starts, and Abigail Cresse returns after 20. Four transfers arrived, headlined by outside Kaleigh Meritt at 4.125 points per set and setter Rylee Sloss at 2.774. The projection is 21.37 wins with a 50.4% chance at the Atlantic 10 title and 58.8% tournament odds.

DePaul.summary: DePaul brings back 76% of its production and four of six starters from a 14-13 season, including its top four scorers: Kendall Timme (3.859 points per set), Isabela Tavares Salomon (3.611), Morgan Stewart (3.224) and Jade Dudley-Epps (2.985). The hole is in the middle, where Katelynn Oxley (277.0 points) and Meghan Scholz (117.5, now at San Diego) both departed, leaving one vacancy in the starting six. Projections put the Big East team at 11.06 wins with a range of 5 to 17, and 5.9% tournament odds, up to No. 132 from a final 2025 rank of 160.

Delaware.summary: Delaware brings back its top six scorers, including outside hitter Anna Logan Gillens at 3.473 points per set and Asia Murray at 2.371, with 65% of its production returning and four of six starters back. The two holes are at opposite and middle, where Dylan Norris (215.5 points in 2025) and Sila Ozyurek (114.0) departed, and only one transfer arrived to fill them. After an 8-17 season and a No. 259 RPI finish, the projection is 9.58 wins with a range of 4 to 16, and the CUSA rank moves only from 262 to 258.

Delaware St..summary: Delaware St. brings back its top three scorers — Aaliyah Mitchell (3.125 points per set), Emma Patmon (2.534) and Hannah Sanders (1.856) — after a 12-18 season, which is the core of 55% returning production. The losses are concentrated in two starting spots: outside hitter Gerren Tomlin (398 points, off to Alabama A&M) and middle Kelsie Dawson (192 points) both started 24 matches, leaving two holes in the starting six with four starters back. Three transfers arrive, two with no Division I record, to fill in around an offense that ran a 5-1 last year. The projection is 15.1 wins with a range from 8 to 22, and 12.1% tournament odds.

Drake.summary: Drake has to rebuild half its front row: three of six starters departed, including Macy Daufeldt (452.5 points in 2025) and Kacia Brown (426.0), leaving 50% returning production and three starting-six vacancies. Setter is also open with Addison Beagle gone after 26 starts. The returning core is real, though — Caroline Smith (2.331 points per set) and Bliss Beck (2.22) are both back, and transfers Matthea Dalton (2.068) and Hannah Ditsworth (1.864) arrive to fill gaps. After an 18-12 season and a No. 64 final RPI, the projection is 17.67 wins with a 25.0% shot at the tournament.

Duke.summary: Duke brings back 84% of its production and five of six starters after a 5-26 season, so the roster continuity is the story rather than the results. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Ngozi Iloh left after 246 points and 30 starts. Both leading scorers return in the pins: Ashby Zubchevich at 3.706 points per set and Taylor Williams at 3.527, with Williams having started 30 matches. The projection is 9.62 wins, up from a final 2025 rank of 225 to 203.

Duquesne.summary: Emersen Schrom returns as the offense's centerpiece at 5.037 points per set, and she is one of four starters back from a 31-match 2025 lineup, along with setter Chloe Wilmot in the 5-1. The two vacancies are real ones: outside hitter Carsyn Henschen (341.5 points) and middle Ariel Helm (320.0) both started all 31 matches and are gone, with only one transfer in to replace them. Returning production sits at 64 percent, and the projection is 16.96 wins after an 18-13 season, with a range from 10 to 24. The Atlantic 10 title odds are 6.6 percent and tournament odds 9.6 percent.

ETSU.summary: Makayla Bays comes back after scoring 4.482 points per set, more than double the next returner, but the middle is gutted: Whitley Rammel (339.5 points) and Brianna Cantrell (311.0) are both gone, along with opposite Isabelle Iosua (234.5). That leaves three of six starting spots open and 54 percent of production returning from a 23-7 season out of the SoCon. The projection is 17.56 wins with a range from 11 to 24, and 26.6 percent odds of reaching the tournament. Only one transfer arrives, so the replacements will mostly come from the 10 players already on hand.

East Carolina.summary: Five of six starters return for East Carolina, along with 76% of last year's production and the top six scorers from a 12-15 season. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Carlia Northcross started 26 matches and scored 222.0 points in 2025. The returning core is led by outside hitter Ellie Pate at 3.912 points per set, with Aulie Huff at 3.046 and Sydney Buchanan at 3.007. The projection is 12.68 wins with a range of 6 to 20, and a rank of 147 after finishing 178th.

East Texas A&M.summary: No 2026 roster has been published yet, so every 2025 starter — including MB Brooke Box, OH Gracie Campbell and setter Haley Mullaney, each with 28 starts — is currently unaccounted for. That group ran a 5-1 to a 9-19 record, with a lineup known in 28 matches and an RPI of 251 to close the year. The projection system lands on 9.52 wins for 2026, with a range from 4 to 15, and puts Southland title odds at 0.7 percent. The ranking barely moves, from 266 at the end of 2025 to 261 now.

Eastern Ill..summary: A 24-8 season is being rebuilt around two returning starters, with four spots in the starting six open after eight departures. Destiny Walker (499.0 points, now at Virginia Tech), setter Catalina Rochaix and middle Emma Schroeder are all gone, leaving 29 percent of production back. Katie Kopshever anchors what remains at 3.468 points per set, with middle Anaya Rawlinson (30 starts) the other returning starter. The projection is 14.54 wins with an 18.9 percent tournament chance, a drop from the No. 132 finish in 2025 to No. 176.

Eastern Mich..summary: Fourteen players departed and only four return, leaving five of six starting spots vacant and just 25% of production back. The losses are top-heavy: outside hitter Ava Siefke (456.5 points in 2025, now at Toledo) and middle Hatteras Welker (373.0 points, now at Coastal Carolina) both started all 31 matches. AshleeKay Christensen (2.683 points per set) and Taeley Mahler (2.134) are the returning scorers of note, with three transfers in and ten newcomers who have no Division I record. After a 13-18 season, the projection is 12.92 wins with a range of 6 to 20.

Eastern Wash..summary: The top six scorers from a 3-25 season are all back, led by outside hitter Kalista Lukovich at 3.636 points per set and Quincy Moran at 2.741, which is why returning production sits at 68 percent. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: setter Anna Bolich, who started 27 matches, is gone to Fresno St., along with Alyssa Radke and Quincey McCoy, leaving three of six starting spots open. With no transfers in and five newcomers who have no Division I record, the rebuild of the setter position runs through unproven bodies. The projection is 6.84 wins in the Big Sky, up slightly in rank from 320 to 313.

Elon.summary: Every one of the top six scorers from last season is back, led by Anna Sewell at 2.914 points per set and Cameron Lanier at 2.614, and four of the six primary starters return. The losses are concentrated on the pin: Simrin Carlsen (249.5 points) and Clara Simmons (216.5) both started at outside hitter and both are gone, leaving two holes in the starting six. With no transfers in and four newcomers who have no Division I record, the rebuild is internal after a 7-20 season. The projection is 9.84 wins, with a range from 4 to 17.

Evansville.summary: The middle blocker tandem of Chloe Cline (2.288 points per set) and Sabrina Ripple both return after starting 22 and 21 matches, and all six of the team's top scorers are back, including Ryan Scheu at 2.254 points per set. Even so, three of six starting spots are open after the departure of Hinsley Everett, who scored 299.5 points in 2025, along with setter Kora Ruff. Evansville brings back 66 percent of its production from a 6-22 season and one incoming transfer, with four newcomers who have no Division I record. The projection is 10.03 wins, with a range of 5 to 16.

FDU.summary: Three outside hitters left after an 18-12 season, including Kylie Nott (324.0 points), Giorgia Vaschetti (248.5) and Avery Bain (228.0), leaving four vacancies in the starting six and just 35% returning production. What comes back is the setter and the middles: Isabella Scarfone started 26 matches, Alessia Zampieri started 23 and scored 2.265 points per set, and Ava Deguzman leads the returners at 2.353 points per set. With only one transfer in and four newcomers without a Division I record, the projection lands at 18.02 wins with a range of 11 to 25 and a 34.1% chance at the NEC title.

FGCU.summary: All six of the top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Julija Grubisic Cabo at 3.483 points per set and Katie Gielas at 2.935, with middle Abby Toeniskoetter at 2.507 — yet only 8 players return against 10 departures, and returning production sits at 59%. The biggest hole is Barbara Koehler, an outside who scored 373 points in 2025. After a 19-9 season and a final RPI of 69, the projection is 11.11 wins with a range of 6 to 16, and a 30.4% chance at the ASUN title.

FIU.summary: Almost the entire 20-12 roster is gone: 13 players departed against 2 returning, leaving just 16% of production and one of six starters back. Jillian Huckabey, an outside hitter who started 27 matches and led the team at 2.752 points per set, is the lone holdover of consequence, with Kira Givans (437.0 points) and Rebekah Pfefferkorn (294.5) among the departures. The rebuild leans on 5 incoming transfers and 8 newcomers without a Division I record, and the projection reflects it at 19.86 wins with a range from 14 to 25. Tournament odds sit at 26.6% and the CUSA title chance at 19.2%.

Fairfield.summary: Fairfield returns its top six scorers from a 25-6 season, led by Mamie Krubally at 3.306 points per set and Emma Bortolotti at 2.631, yet still has three starting-six vacancies to fill after losing outside hitter Allie Elliott, middle Maya Walker and setter Abby Jandro, all of whom started at least 28 matches. The setter spot is the obvious question: with no transfers in and seven newcomers without a Division I record, the 5-1 offense from last year has to be rebuilt around a new distributor. Returning production sits at 64 percent, and the projection is 21.78 wins with a range of 16 to 26, plus a 56.8 percent shot at the MAAC title.

Fla. Atlantic.summary: The Owls bring back their top three scorers by points per set — Olivia Hart at 4.226, Anna Hartman at 3.0 and Libby Ashline at 2.601 — which is most of the 70% returning production from a 19-11 season. The gaps are elsewhere: three of the six main starters departed, including setter Victoria Hensley, who started 20 matches in a 5-1 system, and outside hitter Kayla Richardson, whose 228.5 points were the largest single loss. Two transfers arrive with scoring history, led by Brooke Crummel at 2.091 points per set. The projection is 15.97 wins in the American with a 15.1% shot at the tournament, up from a final 2025 rank of 85 to 69.

Florida.summary: Florida rebuilt the middle of its lineup rather than the edges: 7 transfers arrived while 4 players departed, including MB Jaela Auguste (378.5 points in 2025) to Wisconsin and setter Alexis Stucky (123.0 points) to Penn St. That leaves 3 of six starting spots vacant, though 12 players return and returning production sits at 71 percent. The scoring board is a mix of holdovers and imports — Jordyn Byrd at 4.276 points per set, transfer Logan King at 4.18, transfer Kamryn Chaney at 4.008. After a 16-12 season and a No. 34 final RPI, the projection is 14.11 wins with a 56.0 percent chance at the tournament.

Florida A&M.summary: Almost everything comes back here: 88% of production, 13 players, and five of six starters, with the top six scorers all returning. The one real hole is at outside hitter, where Yaricel Rodrigeuz (174.0 points in 2025) started 18 matches and departed; LaDonna Trantham (3.323 points per set) and Farah Farooq (3.091) headline what's left in the 5-1. After a 14-17 season, the projection is 14.14 wins with a range of 8 to 20, and an 7.6% shot at the SWAC title.

Florida St..summary: Florida St. brings back its top six scorers, led by outside hitter Kyleene Filimaua at 4.35 points per set and middles Nenu Kpea (2.235) and Delaney Ewing (1.851), with 70% of production returning. The holes are specific rather than broad: setter Lily Nicholson, who started 24 matches and transferred to Texas A&M, and outside hitter Iane Henke, the team's biggest loss at 487 points in 2025, leave two vacancies in the starting six out of six. After a 16-13 season and a final RPI of 62, the projection is 18.27 wins with a range of 11 to 25 and a 42.2% chance at the tournament.

Fordham.summary: All six of the top scorers from last season are back, led by outside hitter Erynn Sweeney at 2.858 points per set and Mila Micunovic at 2.539. The losses are concentrated in two outside hitters, Audrey Brown (340.5 points) and Zoe Talabong (228.5), which leaves two holes in a starting six that otherwise returns four players, including setter Whitney Woodrow after 28 starts in the 5-1. With 63 percent of production returning, no transfers in and four newcomers without a Division I record, the roster is essentially internal development after a 9-19 finish. The projection is 11.66 wins with a range of 5 to 19.

Fresno St..summary: Five of six starters return for Fresno St., including outside hitter Jenna Legault, who started all 28 matches and led the team at 3.675 points per set. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Addison Haluska departed after 483 points in 2025 and 28 starts. Returning production sits at 60 percent, with the top six scorers from last season all back. After a 7-22 finish, the projection is 6.7 wins with a range from 2 to 13.

Furman.summary: All six players who logged starts last season are back, and 93% of the production returns from a 21-9 team, with no transfers added. Tennyson Gorman (3.387 points per set) and Ashley Stein (2.972) anchor a returning top six that also includes Lauren Haynes at 2.986, while the biggest departure is middle Grainne McGrath and her 92.0 points. The main open question is setter: Emily Navarro started 22 matches in the 5-1, but both backup setters left. The projection is 17.41 wins with a 17.6% shot at the tournament, and a move up to 114 in the rank after finishing 164.

Ga. Southern.summary: Georgia Southern ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a very stable lineup: setter Kirsten Barrett, plus outsides Reagan Barth and Sam Bowron, each started all 28 matches with a known lineup, with middles Lydia Seymour (27) and Alex Myers (26) close behind. That group went 19-9 and finished 124th in RPI, better than its 98th place in our final 2025 rank. No roster information is available yet for 2026, so every one of those starters is currently unaccounted for. The projection is 17.38 wins with a range of 10 to 24, a 35.5% tournament chance and 10.8% odds of a Sun Belt title.

Gardner-Webb.summary: Gardner-Webb brings back 78% of its production and four of six starters after an 11-19 season, with the top six scorers from 2025 all returning, led by Nicole Osborne at 2.674 points per set and Haedyn Crumbley at 2.665. The holes are at setter and middle: Sloane Rooney (16 starts) and Brookelyn Nance (13 starts) are gone, leaving two starting-six vacancies, though Milla Lugo (30 starts) and Olivia Lefebvre (15 starts) are back. Serena Kohler, who scored 206 points, is the biggest departure. The projection is 12.87 wins with a range of 5 to 21, and a 2.1% chance at the Big South title.

George Mason.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every 2025 starter — including middle Meredith Brown, who started all 30 matches, and outside hitter Avery Booker at 27 — is listed as unaccounted for rather than returning or departed. The 2025 group went 17-13 out of a 5-1 system and finished 146th in RPI. The projection for 2026 is 16.91 wins with a range from 10 to 24, alongside a 9.0 percent tournament chance and 6.8 percent odds of an Atlantic 10 title.

George Washington.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet for George Washington, so every 2025 starter — including MB Sydney Hasenfratz (29 starts), OH Alexis Rodriguez (28) and setter Abby Markworth (24) — is listed as unaccounted for rather than confirmed back. The 2025 season produced a 19-12 record out of a 5-1 offense, with a final RPI of 132 and a year-end ranking of 140. The 2026 projection is 16.75 wins, with a range from 9 to 24, and the Atlantic 10 title odds sit at 8.4 percent against 11.0 percent tournament odds.

Georgetown.summary: Georgetown brings back all six starters and 98% of its production, an unusually intact roster after a 14-15 season. The returning group includes the top six scorers, led by outside hitters Dionna Mitchell (3.339 points per set) and Samantha Soderlund (3.061), with middle Kamryn Lee-Caracci (2.837) behind them in the 5-1. The main departure is middle blocker Vaughan Anoa'i, who accounted for 25.5 points in 2025. Projections put the Hoyas at 10.4 wins with a rise from 159th to 109th in our rank, and 3.6% tournament odds.

Georgia.summary: Bianna Muoneke is back after leading the attack at 4.495 points per set, and she headlines four returning starters from a 16-10 season. The two holes are at middle and on the left: MK Patten (274.5 points) and Estelle Haugen (191.5) are gone, leaving 2 starting-six vacancies and 54% of production returning. Kendal Kemp (2.061 points per set) and Tori Harper (1.927) give the front row experience, with transfer Alyssa Worden arriving at 2.15. The projection is 12.4 wins with a 19.8% tournament chance.

Georgia St..summary: Georgia St. is essentially rebuilding from scratch after an 18-10 season: 16 players departed, only 3 return, and 22% of production is back. Five of the six primary starting spots are open, with middle blocker Akira Burt (13 starts, 2.846 points per set) the lone returning starter. The rebuild is being staffed by 5 transfers in and 8 newcomers with no DI record. Projections put the Panthers at 16.2 wins with a range of 9 to 23, and 12.6% tournament odds.

Georgia Tech.summary: Nine players departed and no transfers came in, leaving 7 returners, 46% of returning production, and zero of last year's six primary starters listed as back. The exits are concentrated on the pins: Lameen Mambu (345.0 points) went to Purdue and Noemi Despaigne (266.0) to Houston, with MB DeAndra Pierce (232.5) also gone, opening 3 starting-six vacancies. Anna Fiedorowicz (3.569 points per set), Larissa Mendes (3.083) and Bianca Garibaldi (2.953) are the returning scorers to build around, alongside 7 newcomers with no DI record. After a 16-14 season and a No. 48 final RPI, the projection is 16.1 wins with a 45.1% tournament chance.

Gonzaga.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after six departures, led by outside hitter Sjakkie Donkers (477.0 points in 2025, now at Oregon) and fellow OH Autumn Larson (229.5) and middle Fallon Thompson (228.5). Only 35% of production returns, though middles Taylor Walsh (2.116 points per set, 29 starts) and Dani Johnson (1.665) are both back, and transfer OH Claire Wagstaff arrives as the highest scorer on the roster at 2.247 points per set. Seven newcomers have no Division I record. After a 14-15 season, the projection is 13.0 wins with a range of 7 to 20.

Grambling.summary: Grambling brings back 70% of its production and four of six starters, including outside hitter Kenya Lucas at 2.994 points per set and middle Rihianna Brown at 2.09. The losses are concentrated in the middle: Ra'Niya Brown (163.5 points in 2025) and Morgan Munro (70.5) are both gone, leaving two vacancies in the starting six. After a 7-19 season and a final SWAC-era ranking of 341, the projection is 8.94 wins with a range of 4 to 14.

Grand Canyon.summary: Five of six starters are back, with the one vacancy coming on the outside where Anaelena Ramirez started all 30 matches and scored 422.5 points. The two transfers in are penciled in as the top two scorers, Katie Schulz at 3.72 points per set and Starr Williams at 3.446, ahead of returning setter Bella Nunez at 2.832. Grand Canyon went 17-13 last season with an RPI of 87, and the Mountain West projection is 15.89 wins in a range from 9 to 23, with NCAA tournament odds at 13.6 percent.

Green Bay.summary: Green Bay brings back five of six starters and 70% of its production from an 11-19 season, with the top six scorers all returning, led by middle blocker Diane Pichelman at 3.73 points per set and outside hitter Gillian Koning at 3.136. The one real hole is setter: Emma Johnson started all 30 matches in the 5-1 and departed, and there are no incoming transfers, only seven newcomers without a Division I record. Libero Katie Schulz, who left for Grand Canyon, was the biggest loss at 346 points. The projection is 15.37 wins with a range of 9 to 22, and a 9.5% shot at the tournament.

Hampton.summary: Hampton brings back four of six starters and 75% of its production after a 1-26 season, an unusual amount of continuity for a team at the bottom of the CAA. The returning group is led on offense by outside hitters Racquel Frazier (2.948 points per set) and Katerina Pappa (2.727), with middle Kylah McNeal (88.0 points in 2025) the main departure among seven players lost. One transfer arrives, middle Janiah Robinson, who scored 2.37 points per set. The projection is 2.03 wins, with a range of 0 to 5.

Harvard.summary: Harvard brings back its entire top-six scoring group, led by outside hitter Sofia Rossi at 3.635 points per set and middle Ryleigh Patterson at 2.981, and returns 66% of its production with 10 players back. The losses are concentrated in two full-time starters: OH Brynne Faltinsky (243.5 points in 2025) and MB Taylor Larkin (132.0), each of whom started all 22 matches with a known lineup, leaving two holes in the starting six. With no transfers in and a 7-15 record last season, the projection is 10.01 wins in a range of 5 to 15.

Hawaii.summary: Hawaii returns its setter-outside core intact: Adrianna Arquette (29 starts), Miliana Sylvester (29) and Cha'lei Reid (28) are all back, with Reid the leading scorer at 4.18 points per set in the 5-1. The losses are concentrated in the front row, where Bri Gunderson (311.5 points in 2025) and Tyla Reese Mane (223.0) leave three of six starting spots open. Three transfers in include Marnie Ursem (2.658 points per set) and Panna Ratkai (2.5), which helps explain 52 percent returning production off a 12-17 season. The projection is 12.43 wins with a range of 5 to 20, and a 5.1 percent tournament chance.

High Point.summary: High Point brings back both middles who led it in scoring, Maya Bukovcan at 2.933 points per set and Addison Freeland at 2.861, and each started all 28 matches in the 5-1. The turnover is concentrated on the pins: outsides Élodie Lalonde (350.5 points), Gia Padilla (148.5) and Brooke Jeffrey (55.0) are gone, leaving two starting-six vacancies with four starters back and 62 percent of production returning. Setter Remy Catojo returns after 23 starts, and returning outsides Gabby Hill (2.274) and Ryley Boyne (2.201) are the in-house options to fill those spots. After an 18-10 season and an 85 RPI, the projection is 16.66 wins with a 47.2 percent tournament chance.

Hofstra.summary: A 22-4 season is followed by a near-total rebuild of the front line: five of the six starting spots are vacant, with eight players gone and no transfers in to replace them. The losses are concentrated at outside hitter, where Izadora Stedile (398.5 points) and Clara Bal (249.0) both departed, along with setter Nina Jioshvili-Ravva, who went to South Fla. What is left is Beatriz Braga, the top scorer at 4.343 points per set, plus Constanza Perez Sain at 2.911, and 47 percent of the production overall. The projection is 17.8 wins with a range of 13 to 22, and a 45.7 percent chance at the tournament.

Holy Cross.summary: Holy Cross brings back 15 players and 77% of its production, including four of last year's top six starters, after a 9-23 season. The two departures that matter are setter Katie Russell, who started 27 matches, and outside hitter Taliah Lee, who put up 338 points before transferring to Weber St., leaving two starting-six vacancies. Emma Sorensen returns as the leading scorer at 3.45 points per set, with three middle blockers — Kyla Harris, Lacey Murphy and Isa Glover — all back and each above 1.8 points per set. Idaho.summary: Four of the six primary starters are back, including outside hitter Kiana Greer, who led the team at 3.574 points per set, along with Sarah Sullivan (1.969) and middle Koen Makaula (1.958), who started all 28 matches with a known lineup. Indiana.summary: Indiana returns its top four scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Jaidyn Jager at 3.965 and middle Ella Boersema at 2.655, but must fill three of six starting spots after losing Candela Alonso-Corcelles (465.0 points in 2025), Avry Tatum (405.5) and Madi Sell (132.5). Indiana St..summary: Almost everything comes back: 14 players returning, 84% of production, and five of six starters, with the only real hole at middle after Kimora Whetstone's 198.5 points. Iowa.summary: Iowa has to rebuild four of its six starting spots, including setter Claire Ammeraal, who started all 32 matches before departing, and 438.5-point outside hitter Chard'e Vanzandt. Iowa St..summary: Iowa St. returns its top six scorers by points per set — led by Alea Goolsby at 3.5 and Nayeli Ti'a at 2.806 — yet only 2 of six starting spots are filled by returners, leaving 4 vacancies in the starting lineup. Jackson St..summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every returning-player question is open: the six most-used starters from last season — outside hitters Jayden James (15 starts), Cierra Gilbert (14) and Katejion Robinson (12), setters Karys Dove (13) and Naija Gadis (9), and middle Kamiera Watkins (10) — are all unconfirmed. James Madison.summary: All six starters are back from a 22-9 season, and returning production sits at 96 percent — the roster loses only three players, headlined by setter Rebecca Watkins and her 56.0 points in 2025. Kansas.summary: Kansas lost its entire outside hitter rotation from a 24-11 season, with Jovana Zelenovic (485.5 points, now at Miami (FL)), Rhian Swanson (377.5) and Selena Leban (177.0) all gone. Kansas City.summary: The top four scorers from a 3-26 season are all back, led by Ryanne Wattree at 2.317 points per set and Emry Brown at 2.287, yet the roster still has 3 starting-six vacancies after 7 departures. Kansas St..summary: Kansas St. returns just one of its six 2025 starters, libero Caleigh Ponn, with five spots in the starting lineup open and only 16% of production coming back. Kennesaw St..summary: Kennesaw St. brings back a middle-heavy core: Olivia Burrage (3.044 points per set), Haley Patterson (2.417) and Maggie Byrd (1.511) all return, along with setter Kaeley Walz, giving the team four of six starters from a 19-9 season. Kent St..summary: Kent St. brings back five of six starters and 69% of its production after an 8-21 season, including setter Christina Vigil, who started all 27 matches in the 5-1. Kentucky.summary: Kentucky brings back five of six starters from a 30-3 season, including outside hitter Brooklyn DeLeye (5.06 points per set) and middle Lizzie Carr, with 64% of its production returning. Lamar University.summary: Lamar University brings back its setter and its top scorer but has to fill four spots in the starting six, with only 2 of six starters returning after 7 departures. Le Moyne.summary: All six of the top scorers from a 4-24 season are back, led by Branwyn Lupton at 2.948 points per set and Nina Salas at 2.568, and returning production sits at 67 percent. Le Moyne enters the NEC ranked 342nd with a projection of 5.37 wins on a range of 1 to 10, and nine of the newcomers have no Division I record.

Lehigh.summary: Nearly everything comes back here: 86% of production, 13 players and five of six starters, with the only real hole at middle blocker after Madison McCartney and her 205 points departed. Liberty.summary: Almost everything comes back here: 11 players returning, 87% of production, and five of six starters from a 20-10 season, with the only hole at middle blocker after Zoe Hall's departure. Lipscomb.summary: Lipscomb loses its two biggest point producers in Courtney Jones (392.0 points) and Berkley Mischler (335.0), leaving three of six starting spots open even though nine players return. Long Beach St..summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 22-9 season, with only 31% of production returning. Opposite Logan King, who scored 476.5 points, left for Florida, and outside hitter Elise Agi (375.0) and middle Rhiann Sheffie (266.0) are also gone. Setter Madi Maxwell, a 30-match starter, is back alongside Sidney Hamaker, who led the team at 2.56 points per set. Louisiana.summary: Louisiana returns four of six starters from a 15-11 season, including the entire left side of Grace Sweeney (2.72 points per set) and Marlee Ervin (2.689), plus setter Ryleigh Garis in the 5-1. Louisville.summary: Five of six starters are back, including outside hitters Payton Petersen (3.607 points per set) and Chloe Chicoine (3.601), with setter Nayelis Cabello returning to run the 5-1 from 2025. Loyola Chicago.summary: The middle blocker spot is the whole story here: Ann Marie Remmes (409.5 points in 2025) and Karli Molnau (273.5) are both gone, leaving two vacancies in the starting six. Loyola Maryland.summary: Every one of the top six scorers from last season is back, led by outside hitter Ava Nepkin at 2.806 points per set and Morgan Crawford at 2.211, which is the main reason returning production sits at 65 percent. Manhattan.summary: Manhattan brings back five of six starters and 75% of its production after a 4-23 season, with the top six scorers from 2025 all returning, led by OH Hanna Kaczynska at 3.578 points per set. The one hole is outside hitter Fiona VanDyke, who scored 317 points before transferring to Central Ark. There are no incoming transfers and six newcomers without a DI record, so the roster churn is minimal. Projection is 9.43 wins with a range from 3 to 16, and the MAAC title odds sit at 0.8%.

Marist.summary: Nearly everything from a 10-20 season comes back: 14 players returning, 90% of production, and five of the six regular starters, with only setter Claire Lewis's spot open after she started 18 matches. The scoring core is intact, led by Sara Dasic at 3.655 points per set and Mallory Reck at 3.035, both outside hitters. With no transfers in and three newcomers who have no Division I record, the setter question in the 5-1 will be answered internally. The projection is 11.57 wins and a move up to 293 from a final 2025 rank of 317.

Marquette.summary: Ten players departed and only five return, leaving 17% of production and just one of last year's six main starters — middle Keira Schmidt, who started 26 matches. Marshall.summary: Marshall keeps its top five scorers from a 15-15 season, including Emma Barnett at 3.491 points per set and Beatrice Ciccarelli at 3.088, which is why 75% of its production returns. Four transfers arrived to fill those gaps. The projection is 12.37 wins with a range of 6 to 19, and a move up to 158 from a final 2025 rank of 181.

Maryland.summary: Maryland brings back its top four scorers by points per set — Haley Melby (2.439), Eva Rohrbach (2.232), Sydney Bryant (2.075) and Duru Gökçen (1.582) — but loses the player who carried the biggest scoring load, outside hitter Ajack Malual (457.5 points in 2025). McNeese.summary: No 2026 roster has been published for McNeese, so none of last season's starters — including MB Ava Henry (25 starts), OH D'Nari Mills (21) and OH Kayla Wilson (17) — are yet confirmed back. Mercer.summary: Both outside hitters who carried the pin rotation are gone: Sophia Henry (372.0 points in 2025) to Middle Tenn. and Charlotte Thompson (273.5) to App State, leaving three of six starting spots open. Mercyhurst.summary: All six of the top scorers from last season are back, led by opposite Julia Shepherd at 3.029 points per set and outside Roslyn Guerra at 2.085, which is the core of 66% returning production. With no transfers in and five newcomers who have no Division I record, the setter spot and two other starting jobs are open. Coming off 12-18, the projection is 10.18 wins with a range of 4 to 16.

Merrimack.summary: Every one of the top five scorers from last season is back, led by outside hitter Mckenna Shotwell at 3.172 points per set and Ella Gizmunt at 1.745, yet only three of six starting spots are filled by returners. The three departures — Aubrey Baker (241.5 points, now at Rider), Morgan Thurlow (227.5) and Marissa Kobelski (185.0, now at ULM) — all started at least 24 matches, leaving 48 percent returning production and three vacancies in the starting six. With no transfers in and seven newcomers who have no Division I record, the rebuild of the front row runs through untested players. The projection is 8.69 wins after a 9-18 season, with a range from 3 to 16.

Miami (FL).summary: A 27-6 season is being rebuilt from the ground up: only 21% of production returns, eight players departed, and four of the six starting spots are open. The biggest hole is Flormarie Heredia Colon, who scored 881.5 points in 2025, with Dalia Wilson (307.5) also gone. Five transfers arrived and they immediately headline the scoring chart, led by Jovana Zelenovic at 3.706 points per set and Avery Bain at 2.327, with returning setter Ariana Rodriguez at 1.762. The projection is 19.79 wins with a 61.7% tournament chance, a step back from a 16th-place finish in the 2025 rankings.

Miami (OH).summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every 2025 starter — including OH Molly Creech (31 starts), MB Gentry Warrick (30) and setter Hayden Hicks (24) — is listed as unaccounted for rather than returning or departed.
