The departures are the heart of the 2025 attack: Olivia Keller (379.5 points), Logan Blutreich (206.0) and Valentina Varani (197.0). Transfer OH Nicole Zake arrives as the highest-scoring name on the roster at 3.646 points per set, with returning OHs Hannah Koester (2.141) and Mila Stojakovic (1.991) behind her. After an 8-21 season, the projection is 8.48 wins with a range from 3 to 15.

Penn.summary: All six starters are back from a 12-12 season, and 93% of production returns — the top six scorers, led by Zada Sanger at 3.588 points per set and Ellie Siskin at 3.089, are all on the roster. The departures are outside hitters, headed by Jalen Tennyson's 53.5 points in 2025, but with 13 players returning and no transfers in, this is continuity rather than reconstruction. The projection is 14.0 wins in a range of 8 to 20, with the rank moving from 214 to 178.

Penn St..summary: The pins are back and the middle is gone: Kennedy Martin (6.222 points per set) and Emmi Sellman (2.437) both return, while both departed middles, Maggie Mendelson (285.0 points in 2025) and Jordan Hopp (191.0), take their production with them along with setter Addie Lyon. That leaves three of six starting spots open and 70 percent of production returning from a 19-13 season. Three transfers arrive, including Whitney Lauenstein and Ryla Jones, and four newcomers have no DI record. The projection is 14.6 wins with a range of 8 to 21 and a 42.8 percent tournament chance.

Pepperdine.summary: Pepperdine brings back 84% of its production and four of six starters from a 21-8 season, including the top three scorers in the 5-1: Ella Piskorz (3.316 points per set), Chloe Pravednikov (3.189) and Maggie Beauer (3.142). The two vacancies come from middle Vanessa Polk, who scored 241 points, and defensive specialist Emma McMahon. Transfer addition Astrid Puig averaged 2.902 points per set, and the projection is 17.1 wins with a range of 11 to 22 and a 46.7% chance at the tournament.

Pittsburgh.summary: Pittsburgh brings back its entire scoring core — Olivia Babcock at 5.972 points per set, Blaire Bayless at 2.908 and Marina Pezelj at 1.973 — while losing the spine around them. Setter Brooke Mosher, who started 35 matches, and both middles, Bre Kelley (261.5 points in 2025) and Ryla Jones (157.5), are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open. Returning production sits at 68 percent off a 30-5 season that ended fifth in RPI. The projection is 24.26 wins with a 95.4 percent tournament chance and only a 29.4 percent shot at the ACC title.

Portland.summary: Five of six starters return, including setter Havannah Hoeft and outside Maui Robins, who each started 29 matches and who led the team at 3.418 points per set. The one real hole is on the pins: Lucia Busso (339.0 points) and Elin Larsson (331.5) both departed, leaving 59 percent of production back and one starting-six vacancy. Transfer outside Lillian Lansing arrives having scored 2.111 points per set. The projection is 13.3 wins after a 14-15 season, with a range from 7 to 20.

Portland St..summary: Portland St. brings back its top scorer, outside hitter Alivia Eikenberg, who put up 4.188 points per set and started 25 matches, along with setter Ava Blascziek in the 5-1 system. The losses are concentrated on the pins and in the middle: Tyra Schaub (305.0 points), Naomi White (263.0 points, now at Washington St.) and Sydney Stenson (190.5 points) are all gone, leaving three of six starting spots open. Returning production sits at 51 percent, with 10 players back, six departures and two transfers in. After an 11-17 season, the projection is 13.7 wins with a range of 7 to 21.

Prairie View.summary: Prairie View brings back 87% of its production and its top four scorers, led by outside hitter Kylee Owens at 4.225 points per set and D'Mya Hill at 3.415. The holes are in the middle and at setter: middle blocker Adlene Jideofor (146.0 points in 2025) and setter MaKinzie Taplin, who started 23 matches, are both gone, leaving two vacancies in a starting six that ran a 5-1. After an 18-12 season, the projection is 15.36 wins with a range of 10 to 20 and a 23.1% chance at the SWAC title.

Presbyterian.summary: Five of six starters are back from a 6-20 season, including setter Anisa Dorlouis, who started 24 matches in the 5-1, and the top six scorers all return, led by Julia Yurkovich at 3.005 points per set. Returning production sits at 77 percent, with the only real hole at middle blocker after Elyse Hutchinson's 204.5 points departed. Seven newcomers arrive with no Division I record, and two transfers join them. The projection is 9.96 wins with a range of 4 to 17, and a 2.0 percent shot at the tournament.

Princeton.summary: Princeton brings back its top six scorers from an 18-7 season, led by outside hitter Erin McNair at 3.222 points per set and right side Taylor Clarke at 2.5. The losses are concentrated in two spots: middle Lucia Scalamandre (315 points) and outside Valerie Nutakor (312) both started essentially every match, leaving two holes in the starting six with four starters returning and no transfers in. Returning production sits at 58 percent, and the projection is 13.23 wins with a 27.9 percent chance of reaching the tournament.

Providence.summary: Providence brings back five of six starters and 83% of its production, including setter Miller McDonald and outside Sophia Adkins, who each started all 29 matches in a 5-1 system. Adkins led the team at 4.164 points per set and Macy Taylor added 2.937, with all six of the top scorers returning. The one hole is outside hitter Audrey Kocon, whose 261.5 points went with her to St. Thomas (MN). After a 12-17 season, the projection is 14.25 wins with a range of 8 to 20.

Purdue.summary: Purdue brings back four of six starters and 72% of its production from a 27-7 season, including OH Kenna Wollard at 4.863 points per set and OPP Grace Heaney at 3.656. The two holes come from OH Akasha Anderson (398.5 points in 2025) and MB Lindsey Miller, and the two incoming transfers, Lameen Mambu and Kate Hansen, arrive with scoring profiles of 3.317 and 2.92 points per set. Setter Taylor Anderson returns to run the 5-1. The projection is 17.38 wins with a range of 12 to 23, and a 64.4% tournament chance against an 8.4% shot at the Big Ten title.

Purdue Fort Wayne.summary: Almost everything comes back from a 3-26 season: 87% of production, 10 players, and five of six starters, with middle blocker Jena Medearis (190.5 points) the only significant departure. Riley Rosneck and Trinity Rye both started 29 matches on the outside and led the team at 4.271 and 2.867 points per set, and setter Haiden Means returns to run the 5-1. There are no incoming transfers, so the one open spot in the starting six will be filled internally or by four newcomers with no Division I record. The projection is 7.5 wins, up from a final 2025 rank of 331 to 321.

Queens (NC).summary: Queens (NC) brings back five of six starters and 64% of its production from an 18-12 season, with the only real hole at outside hitter after Mia McMillen's 284.5 points departed. The returning core is heavily pin-driven: Callie DeSchryver (3.011 points per set), Emma Norris (2.982) and Elizabeth Layson (2.855) are all back, along with setter Tyler Peluso from a 5-1 system. There are no incoming transfers and seven newcomers without a Division I record, so the rotation should look familiar. The projection is 11.85 wins with an 8.9% shot at the tournament.

Quinnipiac.summary: The biggest unknown here is the roster itself: only 1 match in 2025 has a known lineup, and none of the six players credited with a start — Asia Belli, Damla Gunes, Elena Giacomini, Ginevra Giovagnoni, Leilani-kai Giusta, Milena Silva — are listed as back for 2026, with no roster on file. That uncertainty shows up in the projection, which sits at 18.5 wins inside a wide 12 to 25 band after a 19-12 season. The 2026 ranking of 216 is a slight step up from a final 229 in 2025, with an RPI of 218. In the MAAC, the model gives a 20.0% chance at the conference title and 20.6% tournament odds.

Radford.summary: Radford keeps its entire top scoring group: all six of last year's leaders in points per set are back, headed by outside hitter Olivia Ryno at 2.684 and Aubrey Hatch at 2.29. The losses are concentrated at setter and in the starting lineup, with Rylee Sloss (227.5 points) and Sierra Moore (164.5) gone and only three of six starters returning. Returning production sits at 63 percent, with nine players departed and nine back plus two transfers in. After a 10-20 season, the projection is 10.31 wins with a range of 4 to 17, and Big South title odds of 2.6 percent.

Rhode Island.summary: Rhode Island brings back 68% of its production and 11 players after a 5-25 season, but three of the six main starters are gone, including outside hitters Emma Vente (221.0 points) and Aerin Bowman (217.5). The returning core is led by Havyn Rolle at 2.762 points per set, with Chloe Abuto (1.904), McKenna Melton (1.87) and Hannah Jonick (1.88) also back in the Atlantic 10 rotation. The lone transfer in, middle blocker Emily Sawyer, scored 2.06 points per set. The projection is 8.16 wins with a range of 3 to 15, and a slight rank improvement from 301 to 289.

Rice.summary: Rice keeps its top three scorers from a 21-10 season — Aaliyah Smith at 2.908 points per set, Arissa Smith at 2.668 and Kellen Dorotik at 2.418 — which is the core of 52% returning production. The losses are concentrated in two spots: Taylor Preston (511.5 points) and Lademi Ogunlana (265.0) both started all 30 matches, leaving two vacancies in the starting six with four starters back. Four transfers arrive, including Amalia Simmons at 2.097 points per set, plus four newcomers with no Division I record. The projection is 18.64 wins with a range of 12 to 25, and a 45.6% chance at the tournament.

Rider.summary: Rider loses its top scorer of 2025 in outside hitter Kiannisha Santiago, who started all 32 matches and produced 515.0 points, along with middle Carley McAleavey (278.5). Even so, four of six starters return, including setter Makenna Mason (31 starts) in the 5-1, and outsides Rylah Robinson (2.577 points per set) and Erynn Gotsch (2.307) are back, with 47% of production returning. The projection is 12.99 wins after a 16-16 season, in a range from 7 to 19, with a 6.5% chance at the MAAC title.

Robert Morris.summary: The outside hitter room comes back nearly intact — Tia Schultz (2.178 points per set), Layla Todd (2.149) and Natalie Stepanovich (2.143) are all returning — but the setter is not, with Kaitlyn Brown gone after starting all 28 matches in last year's 5-1. Jocelyn Jourdan, the team's leading point producer at 426.5, transferred to North Texas, and middle Azra Eric (232.5 points) also departed, leaving three of six starting spots open. Robert Morris returns 48 percent of its production off a 9-20 season and projects for 9.71 wins in the Horizon, with a range from 4 to 16.

Rutgers.summary: Three of the six starters from a 12-20 season are gone, including outside hitter Lexi Visintine (309.0 points) and middle Zora Hardison (285.5 points, now at Michigan St.), leaving three vacancies in the starting six. Aspen Maxwell returns as the leading scorer at 4.018 points per set, with setter Lily Bolen and middle Natalie Robinson also back, and transfer Skylar George arrives having produced 3.422 points per set. Rutgers keeps 51% of its returning production and projects to 13.27 wins, with a range from 8 to 19 and 2.5% tournament odds.

SFA.summary: SFA returns its top five scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Katherine Holtman at 3.41 and Kennedy Jones at 2.735, yet only three of six starting spots are filled by returners. The departures are concentrated at the front row and setter: Camryn Hill (329.0 points in 2025) and Ilana De Assis (269.0) are gone, as is 5-1 setter Jayden Flynn, who started all 13 matches with a known lineup. With 58 percent of production back and one transfer in, the projection lands at 20.09 wins with a range of 15 to 25, plus a 39.7 percent tournament chance and 29.9 percent odds in the Southland.

SIUE.summary: The top six scorers from last season are all back, led by outside hitter Sophie Robinson at 3.396 points per set and Kennedy Pike at 2.332, which is the main reason returning production sits at 64 percent. The departures are real but concentrated: Kyndia Smith (284.5 points) and Grace Nichols (196.0) were both regular starters, leaving two holes in the starting six with four starters returning and no transfers in. After a 12-18 season and a final RPI of 290, the projection is 12.7 wins in the OVC, with a range from 7 to 19.

SMU.summary: SMU has to replace its setter and its top scorer at once: Averi Carlson started all 33 matches at setter and Malaya Jones, who produced 600.0 points in 2025, are both gone, leaving 2 holes in the starting six. The two highest projected scorers, Gabi Placide (5.124 points per set) and Suli Davis (4.971), are both incoming transfers, part of a 4-transfer class, while Jadyn Livings (3.841) leads the returners alongside middles Favor Anyanwu and Natalia Newsome. With 44% of production back from a 27-6 season, the projection lands at 21.92 wins with a range of 16 to 27. Tournament odds sit at 92.2%, but the ACC title chance is only 20.1%.

Sacramento St..summary: Victoria Marthaler is back after scoring 5.381 points per set and starting all 29 matches, and she headlines a group where all six of the top scorers return. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: middle blocker Ashlynn Archer (396.5 points in 2025) and setter Kate Doorn both started 29 matches and are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open and only one transfer in to help fill them. Returning production sits at 61 percent off a 20-10 season, and the projection is 16.46 wins with a range from 9 to 23. Big West title odds are 5.9 percent and tournament odds 8.7 percent.

Sacred Heart.summary: The pin hitters all came back: Ryleigh Short (3.724 points per set), Abbie Hagedorn (3.203) and Lauren Hubert (3.078) each started 30 matches in 2025 and return for 2026. What left was the middle and the setter — Emily Sawyer (239.0 points) and Cristina Montanez (219.5) both departed, along with setter Ava Roodbol, leaving three of six starting spots open with just one transfer in. Returning production sits at 68 percent off an 11-19 season, and the projection is 14.06 wins with a range from 7 to 21.

Saint Francis.summary: A 20-9 season in 2025 came out of a very settled 5-1: five starters — setter Alexandra Sappia, outsides Alyssa Irwin, Kori McClure and Korrin Burns, and libero/DS Chandler Alter — each started all 19 matches with a known lineup, with Hailey Atkins starting 17. The NEC team finished 214th in RPI while our final ranking had it 250th, and it opens 2026 at 243rd. No roster is posted yet for 2026, so none of those starters is confirmed back and the team has yet to play a match.

Saint Mary's (CA).summary: Almost nothing carries over here: 12 players departed against 4 returning, leaving 11% returning production and five of six starting spots open. Anaya Thrower, an MB with 19 starts, is the only returning starter, and the roster has been rebuilt with 6 transfers in plus 5 newcomers with no DI record. The projected scoring leaders reflect that — transfers Maddie Way (1.887 points per set) and Ava Galvan (1.86) rank ahead of Thrower (1.617). After an 11-18 season, the projection is 16.6 wins with a range of 9 to 23 and 13.0% tournament odds.

Saint Peter's.summary: Roster churn is the story here: 15 players departed and only 8 return, with no transfers in and five newcomers who have no Division I record. What did come back is the top of the scoring chart — Valeria Pagan Munoz (2.56 points per set), Karolina T. Rodriguez Mendez (2.522) and Indira T. Benitez Dumeng (2.473) are all returning, though returning production sits at 45 percent after the loss of Sibana González Acevedo and her 297.5 points. Coming off a 7-22 season and a final RPI of 338, the projection is 8.7 wins with a range from 2 to 16. Conference title odds are 0.5 percent.

Sam Houston.summary: Chloe Monson is back after leading the team at 3.87 points per set, and she started all 29 matches a year ago alongside returning middle Chelsea Butler at 2.291 points per set. The losses are real, though: outside hitter Lauren Malone (354.0 points) and setter Avery Fowler, a 29-match starter, are both gone, leaving three of six starting spots open and 56 percent of production returning. Eight players departed against eight returners, with one transfer in and five newcomers who have no Division I record. The projection is 13.44 wins after an 11-18 season, with a range from 6 to 21.

Samford.summary: Samford returns Ally Cordes, an outside hitter who started all 26 matches and scored 4.121 points per set, but almost nothing else from the 2025 attack: 9 players departed, including Kaleigh Meritt (429.0 points), Greer Golden (233.5) and Sydney Waller (167.0). That leaves 4 of the starting six vacant, 2 starters back and 37% returning production, with just 1 transfer in and 7 newcomers who have no Division I record. After a 13-15 season, the projection is 12.91 wins with a range of 6 to 20, and SoCon title odds of 5.7%.

San Diego.summary: San Diego returns four of six starters, including setter Kylie Munday (29 starts) and outside hitter Nemo Beach, who led the team at 4.516 points per set. The losses are concentrated at the pins and middle: Isabel Clark (435 points) and Kali Engeman (314 points, 30 starts) are both gone, leaving two vacancies in the starting six and 54% returning production. Transfer outside Kierstyn Barton arrives having scored 3.996 points per set. After a 25-5 season and a No. 33 final RPI, the projection is 16.83 wins with a 50.4% chance at the tournament.

San Francisco.summary: Thirteen players departed and only three return, leaving five of the six starting spots from last season vacant and returning production at 18%. All three of the biggest losses were outside hitters: Astrid Puig (296.0 points, to Pepperdine), Emilija Arsic (208.0, to Illinois St.) and Crystal Galaviz (197.5). Middle blocker Maeve Bailey is the one returning starter and the leading returning scorer at 2.461 points per set, joined by three transfers in and seven newcomers with no Division I record. After a 7-21 season, the projection is 11.14 wins with a range from 4 to 18.

San Jose St..summary: San Jose St. brings back 86% of its production and four of six starters from a 13-16 season, with the top six scorers all returning, led by Lolohea Fonua at 2.962 points per set and Morgan Graves at 2.808. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Sariah Johnson (74.0 points in 2025) left for UC Riverside and Morgan Castaneda (57.5) is also gone. Setter Fatimah Hall is back after 27 starts in the 5-1, so continuity is real even with 10 departures and just one transfer in. The projection is 12.8 wins with a range of 6 to 20, and a move up to 126 from a final 2025 rank of 173.

Santa Clara.summary: Santa Clara brings back 12 players and 81% of its production from a 17-12 season, including five of six starters in the 5-1 offense. The one hole is at outside hitter, where Layla Truitt started all 29 matches and scored 344.5 points; Cate Shanahan (3.565 points per set) returns alongside Morgan Hayes, Grace Flanagan and Selin Aslayan, so the rest of the scoring is intact. With no transfers in and four newcomers without a DI record, the projection is 15.07 wins in a range from 8 to 22, and a rise from 149th to 121st in our rank.

Seattle U.summary: Ten players departed and only four return, leaving 28% of production and just one of six starters — setter Grace Jones, who started 18 matches. The exits are top-heavy: Madyn Cervellera (426.0 points) went to Washington St., Yasemin Elmas (251.5) to UC San Diego and Petra Fritz (247.0) to San Francisco, all everyday starters. What's left is led by RS Teagan Melton at 2.127 points per set, with three transfers in and seven newcomers who have no Division I record. After an 8-21 season, the projection is 8.88 wins with a range of 3 to 15.

Seton Hall.summary: Seton Hall keeps essentially its whole offense: the top five scorers all return, led by Sadie Reich at 3.783 points per set and Daria Safian at 2.687, with 74% of production back and 10 players returning. The one real hole is middle blocker Asli Subasili, who started all 27 matches with a known lineup and scored 210 points, leaving four of six starters in place and one vacancy. After a 6-21 season and a final RPI of 286, the projection is 9.26 wins with a range of 4 to 15. Only one transfer arrives, so the improvement has to come from players already in the gym.

Siena.summary: Siena keeps its top three scorers from a 14-19 season — Doga Diraz at 3.854 points per set, Gabrielle Wire at 2.891 and Mary Claire Deacy at 2.576 — yet still has three of six starting spots to fill, with Elizabeth Phillips (258.0 points), Ella Treasure and Berra Tok all gone. Returning production sits at 70 percent, helped by six transfers in, two of whom have no Division I record. The projection is 14.77 wins with a range from 7 to 23, and the MAAC title odds are 2.3 percent.

South Alabama.summary: The top six scorers from last season are all back, led by outside hitters Cambria Gaier (4.066 points per set) and Sarah Gooch (3.892), which is the main reason 73% of production returns. The holes are specific rather than broad: setter Anna Loberg and outside hitter Maradith O'Gorman, who led the team with 249 points, both started 27 matches and both departed, leaving two vacancies in the starting six and a 5-1 offense in need of a new runner. After a 15-14 season and a No. 101 RPI finish, the projection is 15.13 wins with a range of 9 to 22, and 15.5% tournament odds.

South Carolina.summary: Five of six starting spots are open after nine players departed, leaving just 26 percent of production returning and only one starter, middle blocker Ava Leahy, back from a lineup she started 26 times. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Alayna Johnson (303 points in 2025) and Nia Hall (299 points, now at Tennessee) both go, along with middle Emily Beeker (216). The rebuild leans on five transfers, headlined by projected lead scorer Olivia Borgman at 2.152 points per set, plus returners Leahy (1.995) and Elise Marchal (1.879). After a 10-16 season, the projection is 12.52 wins with a range of 7 to 19 and a 17.4 percent chance at the tournament.

South Carolina St..summary: Ten players departed and only 7 return, leaving 22% of production and four of six starting spots open. The losses are concentrated at the pins and middle: Kiyah Felder (290 points), Hailey Harris (182) and Robyn White (156) are all gone, and Harris was one of two players to start all 19 matches with a known lineup. What's left is setter Arianna James and middle Jade Robinson, plus incoming scorer Jessika Martinez at 1.537 points per set; 7 newcomers have no Division I record. After a 2-23 season, the projection is 6.62 wins with a range of 3 to 12.

South Dakota.summary: Almost nothing left: 14 players return and 98% of last year's production comes back, with the only notable departure being DS Kamryn Farris (42.0 points in 2025) and no transfers added. The top six scorers are all back, led by OH Lauren Medeck at 4.168 points per set, MB Morgan Bode at 2.995 and OH Ava Ball at 2.932, with two more middles in Amanda Loschen (2.704) and Audrey Nelson (2.327). After a 20-9 season and a No. 72 final RPI, the Coyotes move up to 48th in our 2026 rank with 15.57 projected wins and a 22.7% chance at the Summit League title.

South Dakota St..summary: The top four scorers all return, led by outside hitter Sylvie Zgonc at 4.769 points per set and Madison Burr at 3.452, which is the bulk of 73% returning production. The losses are concentrated in the middle: Sydni Schetnan (283.5 points in 2025) and Annalee Ventling-Brown (160.0) both started at least 26 matches and are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open. After a 23-5 season and a final RPI of 36, South Dakota St. projects for 17.08 wins in the Summit League with a range of 12 to 22.

South Fla..summary: Eleven players departed and only five return, leaving four of the six starting spots open and just 31% of production back. The exits are top-heavy: Maria Clara Andrade (519.0 points), Arianna Beckham (291.5) and Imani Hartfield (210.0) all scored more than the returners who follow Laila Ivey, who led the team at 2.883 points per set. Four transfers and seven newcomers with no Division I record fill the rest of the roster after a 17-13 season that finished 46th in RPI. The projection is 13.7 wins with a range of 7 to 20 and a 29.8% shot at the tournament.

Southeast Mo. St..summary: No 2026 roster has been posted for Southeast Mo. St., so every 2025 starter — Lucy Arndt (11 starts), Ramiri Gardner (10), Marin Johnson (9), Alaina Lester (7), Avery Torrey (7) and Kara Oxenknecht (6) — is currently unaccounted for, and the lineup data itself covers only 11 matches. The 2025 season produced a 21-13 record with an RPI of 165 and a final ranking of 174 in our system, out of a 5-1 offense. The 2026 projection is 18.75 wins with a range of 13 to 24, alongside a 19.6% chance at the OVC title and 22.4% tournament odds. The ranking moves up to 159 for 2026.

Southeastern La..summary: Only one of six starters is back from a 20-9 season, leaving four vacancies in the starting six after seven departures, including India Bennett (314.0 points in 2025) and Alexis Logarbo (289.5). What does return is scoring: Kyra McKelvey at 3.936 points per set and Anne Brauckmiller at 2.177 both stay, and setter Ashley Richardson started all 29 matches in the 5-1. With no transfers in and six newcomers who have no Division I record, returning production sits at 48 percent, and the projection is 16.54 wins with a range of 11 to 22.

Southern California.summary: All six of last season's top scorers are back, led by London Wijay at 3.865 points per set and Abigail Mullen at 3.778, so 81 percent of the production returns despite three of six starters departing. The holes are specific: setter Reese Messer, who started all 32 matches in the 5-1, transferred to Kansas, and middle Rylie McGinest took 208.5 points with her. After a 25-7 season and a No. 15 final RPI, the projection is 16.95 wins with a range from 10 to 23 and a 70.0 percent tournament chance.

Southern Ill..summary: All six players who led the 2025 starting lineup are gone, leaving 6 starting-six vacancies and just 12% returning production from a 13-17 season. The departures include the top three scorers by total points — Kelly Franklin (385.5), Annabelle Sulish (377.5) and Larissa Seger (329.0) — while only 3 players return against 11 departures and a single transfer in. Ella Swansiger, at 2.054 points per set, is the one returning piece with real offensive volume. The projection is 15.27 wins with a range from 9 to 22, and the MVC title odds sit at 2.2%.

Southern Ind..summary: Southern Ind. brings back five of six starters and 79% of its production, including its top five scorers by points per set: Ashby Willis (4.033), Carley Wright (2.95), Leah Coleman (2.765), McKenzie Murphy (1.62) and setter Aysa Thomas (1.021). The lone hole is at middle blocker, where Bianca Anderson's 367.5 points depart, and there are no incoming transfers to fill it. After a 19-13 season and a 142 RPI finish, the projection is 17.63 wins with a range of 11 to 24, and a 28.5% shot at the tournament.

Southern Miss..summary: Southern Miss brings back five of its six regular starters and 76% of its production, including outside hitter Sadie McAda, who started all 28 matches and led the team at 4.25 points per set. The one hole is on the pin, where Brynn Botkin's 322 points from 2025 departed; the rest of the top six scorers, led by middles Elly Stewart (2.28) and Lillie Johnson (2.227), all return. After a 17-12 season and a No. 160 final RPI, the projection is 16.82 wins with a range of 10 to 23, and a 9.7% chance at the tournament in the Sun Belt.

Southern U..summary: Eleven players departed and only six return, leaving five of the six starting spots from 2025 open and just 23% of production back. Outside hitter Zaria Nelson is the one returning starter and the leading returning scorer at 1.974 points per set; the biggest loss is OH Ariana Brown, who put up 505.5 points in 2025. After a 14-17 season, Southern U. is projected for 9.8 wins in a range of 5 to 15, with a 2.4% shot at the SWAC title.

Southern Utah.summary: Southern Utah is rebuilding almost from scratch: 13 players departed and only 2 return, leaving 5 of the six starting spots vacant and just 16% of production back. The one holdover starter, outside hitter Kaitlyn Hoelker, was also the team's leading scorer at 2.077 points per set. The losses include opposite Victoria Zibecchi (255.5 points) and middles Kaitlyn Aleshire (204.0) and Amaya Tobias (201.0), who left for A&M-Corpus Christi and Oklahoma. After a 3-21 season, the projection is 6.79 wins with a range of 2 to 13.

St. John's (NY).summary: The middles are the anchor here: Chloe Bell (2.106 points per set) and Kya Harris (1.464) both return after starting 18 and 16 matches, but four of the six starting spots are open. Setter Erin Jones (351.5 points in 2025) and outside hitters Martina Ghezzi (275.0) and Ella Parker (203.0) are all gone, part of seven departures against six returners and just 34 percent returning production. St. John's (NY) brings in one transfer and five newcomers with no Division I record. After a 10-19 season, the projection is 13.26 wins with a range of 7 to 20.

St. Thomas (MN).summary: St. Thomas (MN) brings back its top two scorers in outside hitters Anya Schmidt (3.643 points per set) and Ellie Gustafson (2.943), both of whom started all 31 matches last season. The holes are at middle and the fourth OH spot: Megan Wetter (394.5 points) and Tezra Rudzitis (426.5) are gone, leaving four of six starters back and two vacancies in the starting lineup. Returning production sits at 54 percent, and the 5-1 setter Morgan Kealy is also back after a 21-10 season. Projections put the team at 14.86 wins with a 26.6 percent shot at the tournament.

Stanford.summary: Five of six starters are back from a 29-5 season, and the top six scorers from 2025 all return, led by Julia Blyashov at 3.517 points per set and Jordyn Harvey at 3.145. The one hole is at outside hitter, where Elia Rubin and her 471 points departed after 31 starts. Returning production sits at 79 percent, with both middles — Erika Sayer (34 starts) and Lizzy Andrew (33) — intact in the 5-1. Stanford projects to 22.82 wins with an 87.2 percent tournament probability.

Stetson.summary: The top three scorers all return, led by outside hitter Zuzanna Bury at 4.614 points per set, with middles Xinlei Yang (2.752) and Kayla Balfour (1.876) behind her. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: setter Nyah Molina, who started 27 matches, is gone along with outside hitters Jenna Simmons (253.0 points) and Lilyanna Parker, leaving three of six starting spots open. Nine players departed against six returning, and seven newcomers have no Division I record, though returning production still sits at 61 percent. After a 9-19 season, the projection is 7.35 wins with a range of 3 to 13.

Stonehill.summary: Stonehill loses its lead scorer in outside hitter Mia Berardino, who accounted for 385.5 points in 2025, but the rest of the scoring column is intact: the next five names on the list, led by Sam Loyd at 2.724 points per set and Abby Farrell at 2.312, are all back. Setter Kendra Sawyer returns after starting all 29 matches in the 5-1, so three of six starters are back and 59 percent of production carries over. After a 6-24 season and a final RPI of 341, the projection is 8.57 wins with a range of 3 to 15. Seven of the newcomers have no Division I record, and two transfers arrive.

Stony Brook.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet for Stony Brook, so every 2025 starter — setter Ava Zamora, middle Ayanna Pierre Louis and outside Kali Moore all started 27 matches, with Mercedes Motton at 21, Quinn Anderson at 17 and libero Carey-Jean Block at 14 — is listed as unaccounted for rather than returning or departed. That 5-1 group went 12-15 and finished 175th in RPI, 198th in our final ranking. The 2026 projection is 12.31 wins with a range of 6 to 19, which reflects the roster uncertainty as much as anything. CAA title odds sit at 4.8 percent and tournament odds at 5.8 percent.

Syracuse.summary: The 2026 roster isn't public yet, so every 2025 starter — including MB Soana Lea'ea (30 starts), OH Gabby Mclaughlin (29) and setter Tehya Maeva (29) in a 5-1 — is listed as unknown for return. Syracuse went 13-17 last season and finished 169th in RPI, 156th in our final rank. The projection nudges up slightly to 141st with 11.18 wins, in a range from 5 to 17, and gives 2.4% tournament odds.

TCU.summary: The outside hitter room is fully intact: Evan Hendrix (4.933 points per set), Becca Kelley (3.301) and Lauren Murphy (2.667) all return, which is most of why 67% of production comes back. The middle is the problem, with Sarah Sylvester (240.5 points in 2025) and Alexis Roberson (182.0) both gone and three of the starting six to replace. Four transfers arrived, led by middle blocker Mia Lee at 2.345 points per set. After a 21-11 season and a No. 20 final RPI, the projection is 14.9 wins with a 60.0% tournament chance.

Tarleton St..summary: The top five scorers from a 16-10 season all return, led by LaNeah Lara at 2.791 points per set and Madison Frank at 2.701, which is a rare amount of offense to keep intact at 59% returning production. The losses are concentrated instead in the starting lineup itself: three of six starters departed, including outside hitter Madison Natori Rice-Locket (261.5 points) and middle Emma Burke (243.0). Three transfers arrive and four newcomers have no Division I record, so the setter spot and the vacancies alongside Frank are the open questions. Projections put the team at 12.39 wins with a range of 6 to 19, and 5.6% conference title odds in the UAC.

Temple.summary: Three of the six primary starters are gone, including outside hitter Leia Harper (398.5 points in 2025) and middle Alyssa Finister (317.0), who started all 31 matches. What comes back is the top per-set scorer, Christiana Greene at 3.906 points per set, plus Olivia Hummel at 2.668 and setter Lexi Yoza, with returning production at 50 percent. The one transfer addition, middle Khenedi Guest, arrives at 2.787 points per set. After a 16-15 season, the projection is 14.72 wins with a range from 8 to 21.

Tennessee.summary: Twelve players departed and only 7 returned, leaving 35% returning production and three vacancies in the starting six. The rebuild runs through the portal: the top three projected scorers — Jalyn Stout (3.849 points per set), Nia Hall (3.36) and Kennedi Rogers (2.962) — are all transfers, with returning middle Chelsea Sutton (2.845) and setter Caroline Kerr (25 starts) as the holdovers. Hayden Kubik, who scored 431 points in 2025, is the largest loss from a 20-8 team that finished 25th in RPI. The projection is 17.5 wins with a 79.0% tournament chance and only a 7.8% shot at the SEC title.

Tennessee St..summary: The middle blocker room and the setter spot both emptied out at once: Maygan Miller-Garcia (264.0 points in 2025) and Aliyah Harris (215.5) are gone from the middle, and setter Sagaia Reilly (148.0), who started 28 matches, departed as well. What remains is the perimeter scoring — Carsyn Stansberry at 1.869 points per set and Melae Lacy at 1.557 both return, part of 3 returning starters of six and 30% returning production. With 10 players departed and 4 transfers in, the projection is 2.16 wins after a 1-30 season.

Tennessee Tech.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every 2025 starter — including OH Bella Powell and setter Jordan Karlen, who each started all 30 matches, and middles Jordyn Milhouse and Tuva Falk at 25 apiece — is listed as unaccounted for rather than returning. Tennessee Tech ran a 5-1 in 2025 and finished 14-17, with an RPI of 235 and a final ranking of 253. The 2026 projection is 11.55 wins with a range from 5 to 19, and the rank sits at 247. SoCon title odds are 2.0 percent and tournament odds 2.2 percent.

Texas.summary: Five of six starters are back from a 26-4 season, including the entire perimeter of Torrey Stafford (5.277 points per set), Cari Spears (3.573) and libero Ramsey Gary, with 82% of production returning. The one hole is in the middle, where Ayden Ames left for Creighton after 207.5 points, and with no transfers in the replacement will come from inside the program. Projections put the team at 17.58 wins in the SEC with a 95.0% tournament probability.

Texas A&M.summary: Texas A&M returns just 24% of its production from a 29-4 season, with four of the six starting spots vacant and only two starters back — libero Addi Applegate and outside Kyndal Stowers. The departures are heavy: opposite Logan Lednicky (534.0 points), middle Ifenna Cos-Okpalla (396.5) and outside Emily Hellmuth (351.0) are all gone, along with the setter who started all 33 matches. The rebuild leans on four transfers, including Natalie Ring at 5.162 points per set and Eliza Sharp at 2.916. Projections put the Aggies at 19.55 wins with a 93.2% tournament chance, and they open 0-1.

Texas Southern.summary: All six of last season's top scorers are back, led by Lauren Battle at 2.13 points per set, Morgynne McQueen at 1.647 and Gracie Lee at 1.611. The departures are concentrated in two starting spots: Gracie Hill (285.5 points) and Kourtni Collier (265.0) are gone, leaving four of six starters returning and 55% of production intact. There were no incoming transfers, so the two vacancies fall to five newcomers with no Division I record. After a 10-20 season, the projection is 10.79 wins with a range of 6 to 16.

Texas St..summary: Only one of six starters is back, setter Anna Blaine, leaving five spots in the starting six open and just 15% of production returning after eight departures. The losses are heavy at the pins and middle: Samantha Wunsch (440.5 points in 2025), Jade Defraeye (315.5) and Nina Moorer (295.0, now at Ole Miss). Four transfers arrived, and two of them, India Bennett (3.413 points per set) and Peyton McKee (3.179), project as the top scorers ahead of returner Britton Finley (2.4). After a 17-12 season and a No. 45 final RPI, the projection is 16.82 wins with a range of 10 to 23 and a 25.3% chance at the tournament.

Texas Tech.summary: Three of six starting spots are open after the departures of Addie Kanouff, Aliyah McDonald and Jasmine Martin, with Kanouff (271.5 points in 2025) heading to Washington and Kallista Jioshvili ravva taking 335.5 points out the door. What's left is still a scoring core: Kenna McKenzie (2.764 points per set) and Reagan Engler (2.727) both return, joined by transfer Gretchen Sigman at 2.734. Returning production sits at 47 percent, and the projection is 9.72 wins after a 10-20 season, with a range from 4 to 16. Six newcomers have no Division I record, which is a large part of why the spread is that wide.

The Citadel.summary: The Citadel went 0-27 in 2025 yet brings back 75% of its production, including four of six starters and its top five scorers — led by outside hitter Rachel Reininger at 3.591 points per set and Gwen Berry at 2.418. The losses are concentrated on the pins and in the middle: Savannah Freeman (109.0 points), Alexa Psotka (78.0) and Sam Barnes (74.0) are gone, leaving two vacancies in the starting six. Middle blocker Luci Lippelgoos started all 26 matches with a known lineup and returns. The projection is 5.38 wins in the SoCon, with a range from 1 to 11.

Toledo.summary: Toledo keeps 78% of its production and 11 players off a 23-11 season, but the hole is at setter: Kelsey Smith started all 34 matches in the 5-1 and led the team with 219.5 points before departing. Three of six starting spots are open, though Sierra Pertzborn (3.244 points per set) and Olivia Heitkamp (3.305) return, and transfer Ava Siefke arrives at 3.836 points per set. The projection is 15.71 wins with a range of 9 to 22, a rise to 76th after finishing 107th, with a 16.5% shot at the MAC title.

Troy.summary: Troy keeps four of six starters but loses the two who played the most, outside hitter Amiah Butler (23 starts, 450.5 points in 2025) and middle Sydney Austin (20 starts, 181.0 points, now at UAB), leaving two holes in the starting six. What returns is the pin depth: Kalina Calvillo at 2.84 points per set and Olivia Kwiatkowski at 2.411 are both back, along with middles Ashlynn Axtell (1.79) and Ella Broadhead (1.531). Returning production sits at 47 percent, and the roster churn is real, with seven departures against one transfer in and six newcomers who have no Division I record. After a 10-16 season, the projection is 14.64 wins with a range of 9 to 20 and a 6.7 percent tournament chance.

Tulane.summary: The pins are the reason to watch here: Avery Burks returns after 4.519 points per set and 26 starts, with Lauryn Mack (2.707 points per set) back alongside her. The middle and the setter spot are the problem — Ava Derbes (253.0 points in 2025) and Sabrina Skyers (179.0) are both gone, part of 10 departures that leave three of six starters returning and 60% of production. Four transfers in and six newcomers with no DI record fill the rest, and the projection lands at 8.8 wins after an 11-16 season.

Tulsa.summary: Three of last year's six regular starters are back, but the two departures that matter most are outside hitter Lauren Eitler (326.0 points) and setter Brayden Hipp, who started all 32 matches and ran the 5-1. What returns is the middle and a lead scorer: Olivia Vance at 3.277 points per set, Jill Hanson at 3.022 and Kat Cooper at 3.0, which is a big part of the 66 percent returning production. After a 25-7 season and a final RPI of 37, the projection is 17.21 wins with a range of 11 to 23 and a 36.6 percent tournament chance.

UAB.summary: The pins are the reason to watch here: Mia Reese (3.333 points per set) and Abby Jones (2.702) both return, along with 4 of the six 2025 starters. The hole is at opposite, where Jorda Crook scored 456 points before leaving for Ole Miss, one of two starting-six vacancies. UAB returns 58% of its production and brings in three transfers, including middle Sydney Austin (1.946 points per set) and setter Rachel McCollum (2.211). After a 13-15 season, the projection is 14.27 wins with a range of 7 to 21.

UAlbany.summary: Almost nothing carries over here: just 8% of production returns, one of six starters is back, and five spots in the starting six are open. The departures include setter Maria Olga Siapani and outside Shynelle Woroniuk, who each started all 26 matches with a known lineup, with Woroniuk's 428.0 points the largest single loss. McKenna Collins is the top returning scorer at 1.286 points per set, joined by two transfers in and three newcomers without a Division I record. After a 14-12 season, the projection is 12.47 wins with a range of 7 to 18 and a 26.4% shot at the tournament.

UC Davis.summary: Five of six starters return from a 21-7 season, including setter Mia Starr and the top two scorers, Breeze Czapinski (3.204 points per set) and Ally Chandler (2.952), with 67 percent of production back. The one hole is outside hitter Jade Light, who started all 28 matches and produced 474.5 points in 2025; with no transfers in, the replacement has to come from within a group that added six newcomers with no Division I record. The projection lands at 17.58 wins with a range from 11 to 24, and tournament odds of 37.4 percent.

UC Riverside.summary: Five of the six starting spots are open after 10 players departed, including Sophia Ewalefo (379 points in 2025), Mia Delahoussaye (219) and Layla Hooks (175); only outside hitter Andrea Brewer, who started 16 matches, is back from the starting group. Returning production sits at 24 percent, the lowest kind of baseline a 5-1 offense can be rebuilt from. Brewer (2.556 points per set) and RS Nicole Hughes (1.976) headline the returners, with three transfers in, two of whom project as top-five scorers. After a 9-19 season, the projection is 7.8 wins in the Big West, with a range of 3 to 13.

UC San Diego.summary: The 6-2 offense means the setters score, and it shows: Ireland McNees put up 3.009 points per set from the setter spot, second only to outside hitter Molly McCluskey at 3.904, and both are back. Four of six starters return, leaving two holes in the starting lineup after middle Jasmine Saran (266.5 points) and outside Maria Fernanda Afonso (251.0) departed, with 56 percent of production retained. The 2025 season ended 6-24 with an RPI of 273, and the projection for 2026 is 12.06 wins on a range of 5 to 19.

UC Santa Barbara.summary: Four of the six starters from a 23-9 season are gone, leaving just 30% of production returning and 10 departures against 9 players back. The biggest exits are outside hitter Eva Travis (424 points, now at Wisconsin), Kiersten Schmitt (339) and middle Layanna Green (334), so the rebuild leans on five incoming transfers, including projected scorers Auburn Tomkinson and Bella Mathis. Returning outside Gabi Martinez led the projected scoring at 3.241 points per set, with setter Milan Rex and Emma McDermott the two holdover starters. The projection is 19.9 wins in a range of 14 to 26, with a 40.2% tournament chance and a slide from 51st to 66th in the rank.

UCF.summary: Avah Armour returns after starting all 29 matches and scoring 4.886 points per set, and she anchors a group that brings back four of six starters and 67% of its production from a 17-12 season. The two departures are both outside hitters, Skylar English (336.5 points) and Reaghan Thompson (253.5), leaving two holes in the starting six for the 5-1 offense to fill. Middles Sasha Cohen (2.29 points per set) and Ella Chapman (2.021) are both back. The projection is 16.64 wins with a 21.8% shot at the tournament.

UCLA.summary: UCLA brings back its top three scorers by points per set — Marianna Singletary (3.262), Maggie Li (2.727) and Eliana Urzua (2.719) — along with setter Kate Duffey, who started 31 matches in a 5-1 system. The losses are real, though: outside hitter Cheridyn Leverette (511.0 points in 2025) and middle Brooklyn Briscoe, who started all 32 matches before leaving for Florida, account for two vacancies in the starting six. Returning production sits at 49 percent, with 11 players back, seven departed and three transfers in, including Jordyn Johnson at 2.195 points per set. After a 19-13 season and a No. 35 final RPI, the projection is 14.87 wins with a 40.8 percent tournament chance.

UConn.summary: Almost the entire starting lineup is gone: 11 players departed, five of the six spots that logged starts are vacant, and only 18% of production returns, including setter Doga Kutlu and OH Emma Werkmeister, whose 496 points led the team. Grace Maria is the lone returning starter after 25 starts, and the rebuild leans on three transfers, headlined by Maja Daca at 3.631 points per set, plus seven newcomers with no DI record. After a 19-9 season and a No. 74 final RPI, the projection is 18.46 wins with a range of 12 to 24 and a 25.5% shot at the tournament in the Big East.

UIC.summary: All six of the players who started most often in 2025 have departed, leaving six vacancies in the starting lineup and just 25% of production returning. The losses are concentrated in the attack: Ayat Amin (318.5 points), Cleo Lorenzo (285.5) and Julieta Sandez (280.0) are all gone, and with zero transfers in, the roster adds nine newcomers without a Division I record. Ana Petrides (2.278 points per set) and Gabi Peter (2.154) are back and will likely have to carry more. After a 17-10 season, the projection is 17.98 wins with a range from 11 to 24.

UIW.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every one of last season's regulars — setter Calissa Allison and middle Vanessa Eregie at 27 starts each, outside hitters Finley Evans and Kyla Malone at 26, middle Kade Thomas at 25 and outside Kitana Tuufuli at 22 — is currently unaccounted for rather than confirmed gone. That leaves the 5-1 the Cardinals ran in 2025 as the main thing on record, alongside a 17-13 finish, an RPI of 135 and a final ranking of 131. The 2026 projection nudges up to 118 with 15.1 wins expected, in a range from 10 to 20. Southland title odds sit at 27.8 percent and tournament odds at 23.9 percent.

ULM.summary: Fourteen players departed and only five return, yet the roster keeps its two most productive scorers: outside hitter Aniya Hall at 3.965 points per set and middle Kenzie Behl at 1.867, plus setter Morgan Howard, who started all 26 matches of the 5-1 in 2025. The losses are all on the pin — Kennedy Plummer (237.5 points), Madison Derden (185.0) and Chavon Weaver (115.5) were the three biggest departures, leaving three of six starting spots open. Four transfers arrive alongside eight newcomers with no Division I record, and returning production sits at 40 percent. After a 10-20 season, the projection is 9.89 wins for this Sun Belt group, with a range from 5 to 16.

UMBC.summary: UMBC brings back 90% of its production and five of six starters, with the only hole at setter after Izzy Ostvig (136.5 points in 2025) departed. The entire scoring core returns, led by outside hitter Jalynn Brown at 4.15 points per set, plus Hannah Dobbs (3.072) and Claudia Llamas (2.995), all out of a 5-1 last season. That continuity moves the projection to 11.11 wins after a 13-12 finish, with a 27.7% chance at the America East title and 24.8% tournament odds. The rank sits at 157 for 2026, up from 192 at the end of last season.

UMES.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet for UMES, so every 2025 starter — including MB Anjola Omolewa (29 starts), OH Karielys Melendez (28) and setter Jayda Hutchins (27) — is listed as unaccounted for rather than returning or departed. The 5-1 offense went 11-18 last season and finished 304th in our final rank and 294th in RPI. The 2026 projection is 11.13 wins with a range of 5 to 17, and the rank has moved to 295. MEAC title odds sit at 2.4 percent with tournament odds of 2.5 percent.

UNC Asheville.summary: Fourteen players departed and only six return, leaving 17% of production and four of the six starting spots open. The three biggest losses were all outside hitters — Kylie Cackovic (345.5 points in 2025, now at Northern Colo.), Albertine van der Goot (281.5) and Ana Djurovic (271.0) — and the rebuild is being handled with one transfer in and five newcomers without a Division I record. What is left is the top of the scoring chart: Addie Brookbank at 2.556 points per set and middle Lydia Pate at 1.727 are both back after a 12-18 season. The projection is 16.07 wins with a range from 9 to 23, and a 9.1% chance at the Big South tournament.

UNC Greensboro.summary: Allie Sweet is the centerpiece here, an outside hitter who started all 28 matches with a known lineup and scored 5.018 points per set. Four of the six starters are back and returning production sits at 60 percent, though the two departures were both outside hitters: McKenna Timmerman (349.0 points in 2025) and Robin Rosser (316.0). The middles are settled, with Connore' Siler-Nixon at 2.145 points per set and Siena Smiejek at 1.902, and setter Gabby Seeds returns from 24 starts in the 5-1. After a 17-12 season, the projection is 16.26 wins with a 12.0 percent chance at the tournament.

UNCW.summary: Eleven players departed and only four returned, leaving five of six starting spots vacant and just 23% of production back. The exits include OH Hannah Forbes (267.0 points in 2025) and MB Marnie Ursem (244.5 points, now at Hawaii); MB Lilly Sullivan, who started 23 matches, is the lone returning starter. Five transfers arrived, and the projected top scorer is MB Courtney Graham at 2.539 points per set. After a 5-21 season, the projection is 10.02 wins with a range of 5 to 16.

UNI.summary: Five of six starters return from a 26-6 season, and 90% of production comes back, including the top six scorers in points per set. Cassidy Hartman (4.638) and Lily Dykstra (4.071) both started all 32 matches on the outside, with setter Reese Booth running the 5-1. The one hole is middle: Lindsay Oldendorf, who accounted for 188.5 points, transferred to Illinois, and with no transfers in, the replacement comes from inside the room. The projection is 20.45 wins with a 71.8% chance at the tournament.

UNLV.summary: Five of six starters are back, and 75% of production returns, headlined by outside hitter Jaida Harris, who started all 28 matches and led the team at 4.181 points per set. The one hole is at outside, where Alondra Alarcon and her 360 points departed after 27 starts. Basia Latos (2.481 points per set), Rheanna Deen-Jackson (2.37) and Brooklynn Williams (2.182) give the 5-1 offense a settled supporting cast, with one transfer in and five newcomers who have no Division I record. After a 13-15 season and a No. 169 final ranking, the projection is 14.6 wins in the Mountain West, with a range of 7 to 22.

USC Upstate.summary: All six of the top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Summer Kohler at 3.894 points per set and middle Kensley Haneline at 2.926, part of 14 returning players and 75% returning production with no transfers in. The main departure is middle blocker Ady O'Grady, who scored 429 points in 2025. After a 14-14 season, the projection is 13.08 wins with a range of 7 to 19, and the Big South title chance sits at 6.5%.

UT Arlington.summary: Nine players departed and only two of last year's six main starters are back, leaving four vacancies in the starting lineup, including setter Mira Ledermueller, who started 24 matches. The biggest scoring loss is outside hitter Jalie Tritt at 370.0 points, with Sophie Ocampo (203.0) off to Troy. What remains is real: outside hitter Camryn McMinn returns after leading the team at 2.724 points per set, alongside Evyn Snook and middle Sophia Krichev, who started all 25 matches with a known lineup. After an 11-14 season, the projection is 10.94 wins with a range of 5 to 18.

UT Martin.summary: Four of last year's six primary starters are gone, including outside hitters Kayla Bryant (352.5 points) and Kylie Surratt (284.5, now at Youngstown St.) and opposite Kristin Phillips (228.0), leaving just 27% of production back. Maddy Gladson, the top returning scorer at 2.016 points per set, started only 12 matches; middle Carly Mueller is the one holdover who started nearly every match, at 27. Four transfers arrive, with Sophie Diouf (1.962) and Luli Arcucci (1.514) the highest-scoring additions. After a 4-25 season and a final RPI of 332, the projection is 8.58 wins with a range of 4 to 14.

UTRGV.summary: Four of six starters are back from a 22-8 season, including outside hitter Martina Franco, who led the team at 4.042 points per set, but the setter spot is open after Isabella Costantini departed for Arizona St. following 13 starts. The other big exit is OH Dimitra Nanou, whose 346.5 points in 2025 went to BYU, leaving two starting-six vacancies and 57 percent of production returning. Two transfers arrived and four newcomers have no Division I record, which makes the 5-1 from last season a question rather than a given. Projection is 17.01 wins with a 20.6 percent shot at the tournament.

UTSA.summary: Five of six starters are back from a 13-15 season, including outside hitter Ally Tribe (3.101 points per set) and middle Caroline Tredwell (2.861), with returning production at 80 percent. The one hole is at outside, where Taylor Gaines left for Louisiana after 269 points. Five transfers arrived to fill in around that group, which ran a 5-1 last season. The projection is 12.89 wins with a range of 6 to 20, and a move up to 124 in the rank after finishing 162.

Utah.summary: Utah has four of six starting spots open after losing middle blocker Emrie Moea'i, who started all 29 tracked matches and led the team with 418.5 points, along with outside hitters Neea-Maria Joki and Levani Key-Powell. Kamryn Gibadlo anchors what returns, at 4.703 points per set and 29 starts, and incoming transfer Loryn Helgesen scored 4.081 per set at opposite. Returning production sits at 52 percent, and the projection is 14.47 wins after a 15-15 season, with a range from 7 to 22. Tournament odds are 33.9 percent.

Utah St..summary: All six starters from a 24-8 season are gone, leaving 2% returning production and a starting six to rebuild from scratch after 10 departures. The roster has been restocked through the portal with 7 transfers in, and the projected top scorers are almost all new: Sami Blackett at 3.574 points per set, Addy Cook at 2.535, and Olivia Ruy at 2.008, with returning middle Ava Napierski at 1.45. The biggest single loss is OH Mara Stiglic (494 points in 2025), followed by OPP Loryn Helgesen (453), who went to Utah. That churn shows in the outlook: a drop from 23rd to 55th in our rank, with 17.04 projected wins and NCAA tournament odds of 52.2%.

Utah Tech.summary: Utah Tech brings back five of six starters and 78% of its production from a 21-6 season, with the only hole at middle blocker after Taylor Snow's 260 points departed. Kennedi Knudsen headlines the returners at 4.85 points per set, backed by Casidy Fried (2.459) and Nana Asiata (2.37), all inside the 5-1 the team ran in 2025. The projection is 19.49 wins with a 27.4% shot at the Big Sky title and 29.6% tournament odds, moving the ranking from 92 to 67.

Utah Valley.summary: Almost the entire lineup turned over: 10 players departed and only 6 returned, leaving 10% returning production and just one of six starters back. That one is Olivia Gloeckner, an outside hitter who started 12 matches and scored 1.974 points per set, while Avery Page (409 points) and Sami Blackett (361 points, now at Utah St.) are gone from the pins. Transfer Miley Thunstrom arrives as the top projected scorer at 2.4 points per set, one of two transfers in alongside four newcomers with no Division I record. After a 16-11 season and a final rank of 108, the projection is 16.64 wins with a range of 9 to 24 and an 11.9% shot at the tournament.

VCU.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 16-13 season, with Julia Rienks (504.0 points), Kalina Pylinska (311.0) and Alicja Jaryszek (244.5) all gone along with setter Elif Ozsoy. What comes back is concentrated in the middle and at opposite: Lara Del Core at 3.628 points per set, Letizia Galli at 2.491 and Nina Boledovicova at 2.277 are all returning, though overall returning production sits at 43 percent. There are no transfers in and six newcomers with no Division I record, so the setter job and both pin spots will be filled from inside. The projection is 15.06 wins with a range of 9 to 21 and a 13.9 percent tournament chance.

Vanderbilt.summary: Vanderbilt went 9-18 in 2025 with an RPI of 118, running a 5-1 offense across 27 matches with a known lineup. Setter Isabella Bareford, middle Jacquelyn Moore and outside Reese Animashaun each started all 27 of those matches, but no 2026 roster has been posted yet, so returner status is unknown across the board. The projection is 12.27 wins for 2026, with a range from 7 to 18, and 17.0% tournament odds. That comes with a move up to 74th in our rank for 2026 after finishing 83rd.

Villanova.summary: All six starters are back from a 20-8 season, and returning production sits at 91 percent, with the only real hole at opposite where Ava Mehrten's 160.5 points depart. Abby Harrell leads the returning group at 4.313 points per set, followed by Campbell McKinnon at 3.51, both of whom started nearly every match in the 5-1. The 2025 finish — 39th in RPI — outpaced the final ranking of 55, and the projection now lands at 32nd with 14.61 wins and a 33.2 percent shot at the tournament. Big East title odds are thinner at 4.9 percent.

Virginia.summary: Three of the six regular starters are gone, including outside hitters Kadynce Boothe (238.0 points) and Jasmine Robinson (164.0) and middle Kate Dean (144.0), leaving 64% of production returning. Reagan Ennist anchors what remains at 4.186 points per set after starting 26 matches, with setter Hannah Scott and Lauryn Bowie also back. Two transfers arrive to fill the gaps, and Emily Fowler brings 3.17 points per set. After a 13-17 season, the projection is 11.85 wins with a range of 5 to 18 and 5.8% Tournament odds.

Virginia Tech.summary: Ten players departed and only 20% of production returns, leaving four of the six starting spots open after a 12-19 season. The losses are concentrated at the pins and in the middle: Payton Woods (366.5 points) left for Arizona, with middles Isabella Mishler (260.5) and Brianna Holladay (224.0) also gone, Holladay to Florida. Setter Camilla Brandalise is back after starting all 30 matches in the 5-1, and outside Reese Hazelton returns as the top returning scorer at 2.176 points per set, with transfer Destiny Walker arriving at 4.455. The projection is 9.44 wins in the ACC, in a range from 4 to 15.

Wake Forest.summary: No 2026 roster has been published yet for Wake Forest, so every 2025 starter — including OH Paige Crawford (31 starts), MB Sanaa Williams (30) and MB Kelis Hawkins (27) — is listed as unaccounted for rather than confirmed back. The 5-1 offense went 15-16 last season with an RPI of 146, finishing 109th in our final 2025 rank. The 2026 projection is 15.35 wins with a range of 8 to 22 and a 10.0% chance at the tournament field.

Washington.summary: Three of six starters are gone, including both outside hitters who led the team in total points, Kierstyn Barton (447.5) and Alexa Markley (393.0), leaving 44% of production returning. Simona Mateska is the returning anchor at 3.477 points per set, with middles Julia Hunt (2.25) and Katy Wessels (2.004) also back. Washington went 13-17 last season and finished 57th in RPI; the projection is 15.14 wins with a range of 9 to 21 and a 37.4% tournament chance.

The rebuild leans on the portal: 7 transfers in, with Emerson Matthews (4.149 points per set) and Madyn Cervellera (3.737) projected as the top two scorers ahead of returning outside Eliana Ti'a (2.75). Lucie Blazkova's 384 points and 27 starts are the single biggest hole to fill. Projections put the team at 12.32 wins with a range of 6 to 19 and a 10.2% tournament chance.

After an 18-12 season and a No. 143 finish, the projection is 17.02 wins with a range of 10 to 23 and a 15.4% chance at the Big Sky title.

West Ga..summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet, so every one of last season's top starters — middles Alex Strating and Sanai Young at 28 starts each, Grace-Blythe Cornett at 26, Valiree Schmus at 25, setter Addy Franz at 24 in a 5-1, and Molly Brunell at 17 — is listed as unaccounted for. That follows a 2-27 season that finished 324th in our rank and 323rd in RPI. The 2026 projection is 7.68 wins with a range of 3 to 13, and the rank barely moves to 322. Conference title and tournament odds both sit at 0.2 percent in the UAC.

West Virginia.summary: All six of last year's top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Nina Horning at 3.364 points per set and opposite Trinity Sheridan at 3.162, and four of the six starters return with 66% of production. The losses are concentrated in two spots: Cassidy Tanton (250.5 points) and Laila Ibrahim (199.5) leave two vacancies in the starting six, and with no transfers in, the eight newcomers have no Division I record. After a 15-15 season in the Big 12, the projection is 12.88 wins with a range of 6 to 20 and 11.0% tournament odds.

Western Caro..summary: Five of the six players who started most often in 2025 are back, including setter Katie Boney, outside Samantha Kranzler and middle Tatum Sharp, who each started 29 matches in the 5-1. That keeps 63% of returning production and the top three scorers by points per set, led by Zoe Zudans at 3.22. The one real hole is in the middle: Courtney Graham, who scored 261.5 points, left for UNCW, and fellow middle Janelle Blue and her 224.5 points are also gone. After an 8-21 season, the projection is 11.19 wins with a range of 4 to 19.

Western Ill..summary: Western Ill. keeps its top six scorers from a 7-24 season, led by outside hitter Kennedy Adair at 2.441 points per set and middle Hillary Estes at 1.653, yet still has three of six starting spots to fill after losing Keyana Cruse (454.0 points), Elizabeth Ziegler (241.5) and Grace Kremer (164.0). Returning production sits at 43 percent, with 11 players back, five departed and no transfers in. The projection is 8.13 wins in the OVC, with a range of 3 to 13, and a move from 319 to 323 in the ranking.

Western Ky..summary: Western Ky. brings back its entire top six scorers, headlined by Kaira Knox at 3.935 points per set and Alivia Skidmore at 3.745, and returns 89% of its production overall. The main hole is at setter: Callie Bauer, who led all departures with 131.5 points in 2025, is gone along with middle Gabby Weihe, leaving two of six starting spots open. After a 27-6 season and a No. 30 final RPI, the projection is 20.86 wins with a range of 15 to 26, plus a 52.8% shot at the CUSA title.

Western Mich..summary: The middle blocker room emptied out: Mary Clare Brusek (391.0 points), Molly Brown (344.5) and Amanda Glanton (240.0) all departed, leaving three of six starting spots open and just 38% of production returning. What is back is the perimeter and the setter, with Annalise Patchett (2.907 points per set) and Mia Jurkovic (2.424) returning alongside Leah Richmond, who started all 31 matches in the 5-1. Two transfers arrive, including middle Gabby Weihe. After a 17-16 season, the projection is 16.3 wins with a range of 9 to 23 and a 16.7% chance at the tournament.

Wichita St..summary: Wichita St. keeps its top six scorers from a 19-11 season, led by outside hitter Sydney Dunning at 4.164 points per set and middle Maddie Wilson at 2.586, with setter Jordan Heatherly back after 30 starts in the 5-1. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Brooklyn Leggett (441.0 points) and Emerson Wilford (233.5) both depart, leaving two starting-six vacancies. Returning production sits at 64 percent, and the projection is 16.92 wins with a 43.9 percent chance at the tournament.

William & Mary.summary: The outside hitter room is the strength here: Audrey Brcka (3.121 points per set), Katherine Arnason (3.01) and Devereaux Hoxsie (2.86) all return. The losses are concentrated elsewhere — opposite Nicole Smith (269.0 points in 2025), setter Beatriz Silva (98.5) and middle Ryann Love (87.0) are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open and 62% of production returning. After a 12-15 season, the projection is 12.32 wins with a range of 6 to 18, and the setter job is the obvious question in a 5-1.

Winthrop.summary: Both opposite starters are gone: Avery Jolley (430.5 points in 2025) and Rachel McCollum (214.5 points, now at UAB) each started all 25 matches, leaving two holes in the starting six. What comes back is the middle and the top scorer, with Paige Bennett at 3.443 points per set, Teagan Sychterz at 2.51 and Giselle Little at 2.26, part of 60% returning production and four of six starters. After an 18-7 season and a final RPI of 111, the projection is 15.83 wins with a range of 10 to 21 and a 30.1% chance at the Big South title.

Wisconsin.summary: Wisconsin returns just 23% of its production after losing four of six starters, including Mimi Colyer (659.0 points in 2025), Una Vajagic (340.5) and Carter Booth (317.0). The rebuild leans on two transfers who project as the top scorers, Eva Travis at 4.417 points per set and Jaela Auguste at 3.505, alongside returning setter Charlie Fuerbringer and outside Grace Egan, each of whom started 24 matches. After a 28-5 season and a No. 6 finish, the projection drops to 19.26 wins with an 87.3% tournament chance and only a 16.6% shot at the Big Ten title.

Wofford.summary: Wofford brings back 82% of its production and 14 players, including four of six starters from a 17-14 season, with the middle-blocker hole left by Annemarie Rakoski (281.5 points in 2025, all 31 starts) the main thing to solve. The returning core is front-loaded: outside hitter Chloe Smith at 3.889 points per set and middles Bradley Brown at 3.375 and Natalie Arnold at 2.403 all come back. The projection is 19.78 wins with a range of 13 to 26, a move up to 97th after finishing 120th, and a 30.9% chance at the SoCon title.

Wright St..summary: Five of six starters return from a 21-11 season, including setter Lauren Yacobucci and middle Reilly Zegunis, who each started all 32 matches in the 5-1. The top four scorers are all back, led by outside Mya Ayro at 4.34 points per set and Katie Sowko at 3.807, giving 72% returning production with no transfers added. The one hole is middle Taylor Bransfield, whose 300.5 points led the departures. Projection is 16.02 wins with a 23.6% shot at the Horizon title.

Wyoming.summary: No 2026 roster has been posted yet for Wyoming, so every 2025 starter — including OH Paige Lauterwasser and MB Sarah Holcomb, each with 30 matches started, and setter Sara Quigley at 22 — is listed as unresolved rather than returning or departed. The 2025 group went 17-13 out of a 5-1, finishing 100th in RPI and 96th in our final rank. The 2026 projection nudges up to 88th with 15.66 wins, though the range from 8 to 23 reflects how little is known. Conference title odds sit at 9.9 percent with tournament odds at 14.1 percent.

Xavier.summary: Xavier brings back five of six starters from a 26-5 season, including the top three scorers in Margo Kemp (2.624 points per set), Charlotte Moriarty (2.433) and McKinley Boehm (2.338), with 61% of production returning. The one hole is on the pin: Emma Grace (429 points) and Anna Taylor (321) are both gone, leaving a single vacancy in the starting six alongside setter Macy Hatkevich in the 5-1. Transfer Iyanna Battle arrives after scoring 1.802 points per set, adding to a front row already stocked with middles. The projection is 17.62 wins with a range of 12 to 23, and a 37.4% chance at the tournament after finishing 27th in RPI.

Yale.summary: Yale returns its top four scorers by points per set — Ava Poinsett (4.234), Laurece Abraham (3.324), Betsy Goodenow (3.008) and Cam Bolane (2.977) — which is the core of 73 percent returning production off a 15-9 season. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: setter Halle Sherlock and two other starters are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open with no transfers in. The projection is 15.51 wins with a range of 11 to 20, a 40.2 percent shot at the Ivy League title and 47.5 percent tournament odds.

Youngstown St..summary: The pins are the story here: Abbie Householder returns after 4.727 points per set and 31 starts, with Layne Graffice (3.0 points per set) back alongside her and setter Kameron Blizniak, who also started all 31 matches in the 5-1. The losses are real, though — Gabriela Machin's 443.0 points and middle Taya Nordmann's 199.5 both walk out the door, leaving three of six starting spots open and 51 percent of production returning. Three transfers arrive, including Kylie Surratt at 2.845 points per set, plus five newcomers with no Division I record. After a 17-14 season and a final RPI of 241, the projection is 14.74 wins with a range of 8 to 21 and a 10.4 percent shot at the tournament.
